title.zh: 卷一百四十九 志第一百〇二 輿服一
title.raw: 卷一百四十九 志第一百〇二 輿服一 Volume 149 Treatises 102: Carriages and Clothes 1

sentences.zh: 輿服一

translations.literal: Carriages and Clothes, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and Clothes, Part One

sentences.zh: ○五輅大輅大輦芳亭輦鳳輦逍遙輦平輦七寶輦小輿腰輿耕根車進賢車明遠車羊車指南車記裏鼓車白鷺車鸞旗車崇德車皮軒車黃鉞車豹尾車屬車五車涼車相風烏輿行漏輿十二神輿鉦鼓輿鍾鼓樓輿

translations.literal: ○ The Five Imperial Carriages, the Great Imperial Carriage, the Great Palanquin, the Fragrant Pavilion Palanquin, the Phoenix Palanquin, the Free-Roaming Palanquin, the Level Palanquin, the Seven-Treasures Palanquin, the Small Sedan, the Waist Sedan, the Plough-Root Carriage, the Advancing Worthies Carriage, the Bright-Distance Carriage, the Sheep Carriage, the South-Pointing Carriage, the Li-Drum Carriage, the White Egret Carriage, the Luan-Banner Carriage, the Honoring Virtue Carriage, the Leather Canopy Carriage, the Yellow Battle-Axe Carriage, the Leopard-Tail Carriage, the Retinue Carriage, the Five Carriages, the Cooling Carriage, the Wind-Measuring Bird Carriage, the Moving Clepsydra Carriage, the Twelve Spirit Carriage, the Gong-Drum Carriage, the Bell-Drum Tower Carriage
translations.idiomatic: ○ Section contents: The five imperial carriages; the great imperial carriage; the great palanquin; the Fragrant Pavilion palanquin; the phoenix palanquin; the free-roaming palanquin; the level palanquin; the Seven Treasures palanquin; the small sedan; the waist sedan; the plough-root carriage; the advancing worthies carriage; the bright-distance carriage; the sheep carriage; the south-pointing carriage; the li-drum carriage; the white egret carriage; the luan-banner carriage; the honoring virtue carriage; the leather canopy carriage; the yellow battle-axe carriage; the leopard-tail carriage; the retinue carriage; the five carriages; the cooling carriage; the wind-measuring bird carriage; the moving clepsydra carriage; the twelve spirit carriage; the gong-drum carriage; and the bell-drum tower carriage.

sentences.zh: 昔者聖人作輿，軫之方以象地，蓋之圓以象天。

translations.literal: In antiquity the sage made carriages; he made the frame square to symbolize the earth and the canopy round to symbolize Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the sages devised carriages with a square frame to represent the earth and a round canopy to represent Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《易·傳》言：“黃帝、堯、舜，垂衣裳而天下治，蓋取諸乾坤。”

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Changes says: "Huangdi, Yao, and Shun let their robes hang down and all under Heaven was well governed—this was surely taken from Qian and Kun."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Changes says, "Huangdi, Yao, and Shun let their robes hang down and the realm was well governed"—a pattern drawn from Qian and Kun.

sentences.zh: 夫輿服之製，取法天地，則聖人創物之智，別尊卑，定上下，有大於斯二者乎！

translations.literal: As for the institutions of carriages and dress, taking Heaven and earth as models—in the sage's wisdom in creating things, distinguishing honor from baseness and fixing high from low—is there anything greater than these two?
translations.idiomatic: The institutions governing carriages and ceremonial dress take Heaven and earth as their model. In the sage's wisdom for ordering the world, could anything surpass these two in marking rank and fixing precedence?

sentences.zh: 舜命禹曰：“予欲觀古人之象，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲作會，宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻絺繡，以五采彰施於五色，作服，汝明。”

translations.literal: Shun charged Yu, saying: "I wish to observe the emblems of the ancients: the sun, moon, stars, constellations, mountains, dragons, and splendid creatures arrayed in assembly; the ancestral vessels, water-weed, fire, powdered grain, fu and fu patterns in fine and coarse embroidery—the five colors displayed upon the five hues to make garments. Make this clear to me."
translations.idiomatic: Shun charged Yu, saying, "I wish to study the emblems of antiquity—the sun, moon, stars, constellations, mountains, dragons, and splendid creatures in full array; ancestral vessels, waterweed, fire, powdered grain, and the fu and fu patterns in fine and coarse embroidery—the five colors set upon the five hues to fashion garments. Bring this to light for me."

sentences.zh: 《周官》之屬，有巾車、典路、司常，有司服、司裘、內司服等職。

translations.literal: Among the offices of the Rites of Zhou were the Director of Carriages, the Director of Roads, and the Director of Banners; there were also the Director of Garments, the Director of Fur Garments, the Inner Director of Garments, and other such posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou list such offices as the Director of Carriages, the Director of Roads, and the Director of Banners, along with the Director of Garments, the Director of Fur Garments, the Inner Director of Garments, and the like.

sentences.zh: 以是知輿服始於黃帝，成於唐、虞，曆夏及商，而大備於周。

translations.literal: From this one knows that carriages and dress began with Huangdi, were completed under Tang and Yu, passed through Xia and Shang, and reached full completion under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that carriages and ceremonial dress originated with Huangdi, took shape under Yao and Shun, passed through Xia and Shang, and attained their full form under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周衰，列國肆為侈汰。

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, the feudal states wantonly practiced extravagance and excess.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined, the feudal states indulged freely in extravagance and excess.

sentences.zh: 秦並之，攬上選以供服禦，其次以賜百官，始有大駕、法駕之製；

translations.literal: When Qin united them, it gathered the finest for imperial service and dress, and distributed the rest to the hundred officials; thereupon the institutions of the grand escort and the statutory escort first appeared.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the realm, it reserved the finest equipage for the emperor's service and dress and distributed the rest among officials, giving rise to the grand escort and statutory escort.

sentences.zh: 又自天子以至牧守，各有鹵簿焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the Son of Heaven down to the prefects and governors, each had his own guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven down to prefects and governors, each rank had its own guard of honor as well.

sentences.zh: 漢興，乃不能監古成憲，而效秦所為。

translations.literal: When Han arose, it was unable to take the ancient completed statutes as its model and instead imitated what Qin had done.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, it could not take the ancient statutes as its guide and instead followed Qin's example.

sentences.zh: 自是代有變更，誌有詳略。

translations.literal: From then on each age had its changes, and the records vary in fullness or brevity.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter each dynasty altered the system, and historical accounts vary in detail.

sentences.zh: 《東漢》至《舊唐書》皆稱《輿服》，《新唐書》改為《車服》，鄭樵合諸代為《通志》又為《器服》。

translations.literal: From the Book of Later Han through the Old Book of Tang all call it "Carriages and Clothes"; the New Book of Tang changed it to "Carriages and Dress"; Zheng Qiao, combining the dynasties in his Comprehensive Records, again titled it "Utensils and Dress."
translations.idiomatic: From the Book of Later Han through the Old Book of Tang the treatise was titled Carriages and Clothes; the New Book of Tang renamed it Carriages and Dress; and Zheng Qiao, in his Comprehensive Records spanning the dynasties, called it Utensils and Dress.

sentences.zh: 其文雖殊，而考古製作，無以尚於三代矣。

translations.literal: Although the wording differs, when one examines antiquity in making things, nothing surpasses the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Though the titles differ, in studying antiquity for craftsmanship nothing surpasses the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 夫三代製器，所以為百世法者，以其華質適中也。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties fashioned utensils and thereby became the model for a hundred generations because their ornament and substance were properly balanced.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties fashioned ritual objects that became the model for a hundred generations because they balanced ornament and substance perfectly.

sentences.zh: 孔子答顏淵為邦之問曰：“ 乘殷之輅，服周之冕。”

translations.literal: When Yan Yuan asked Confucius about governing a state, Confucius replied: "Ride in the carriages of Yin and wear the caps of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Yuan asked Confucius how to govern a state, he answered, "Ride in the carriages of Yin and wear the caps of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 且《禮》謂“周人上輿”，而孔子獨取殷輅，是殷之質勝於周也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Rites say that "the people of Zhou valued carriages," yet Confucius alone took the carriages of Yin—this shows that Yin's substance surpassed Zhou's.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say that "the Zhou valued carriages," yet Confucius chose Yin's carriages alone—showing that Yin's substance surpassed Zhou's.

sentences.zh: 又言禹“致美乎黻冕”。

translations.literal: He also said that Yu "brought beauty to the fu caps and robes."
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Yu "brought beauty to the fu caps and ceremonial robes."

sentences.zh: 而論冕以周為貴，是周之文勝於夏也。

translations.literal: Yet in discussing caps he held Zhou in esteem—this shows that Zhou's refinement surpassed Xia's.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in discussing ceremonial caps he prized Zhou—showing that Zhou's refinement surpassed Xia's.

sentences.zh: 蓋已不能無損益於其間焉。

translations.literal: Surely one could not avoid additions and subtractions in the interval.
translations.idiomatic: Surely additions and subtractions were unavoidable along the way.

sentences.zh: 不知曆代於秦已還，何所損益乎？

translations.literal: One does not know what additions or subtractions the successive dynasties since Qin have made.
translations.idiomatic: What additions or subtractions have the successive dynasties since Qin actually made?

sentences.zh: 宋之君臣，於二帝、三王、周公、孔子之道，講之甚明。

translations.literal: The rulers and ministers of Song expounded the Way of the Two Emperors, the Three Kings, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius with great clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Song rulers and ministers expounded the Way of the Two Emperors, the Three Kings, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius with notable clarity.

sentences.zh: 至其規模制度，飾為聲明，已足粲然，雖不能盡合古製，而於後代庶無愧焉。

translations.literal: As for their scale and institutions, adorned as manifest declarations, they were already splendid enough; although they could not fully accord with ancient models, they would scarcely need to feel ashamed before later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Their institutions and ceremonial display were splendid enough that, though they could not fully match ancient models, later ages would have little cause for reproach.

sentences.zh: 宋初，袞冕綴飾不用珠玉，蓋存簡儉之風，及為鹵簿，又熾以旗幟，華以繡衣，褻以球杖，豈非循襲唐、五季之習，猶未能盡去其陋邪？

translations.literal: In early Song, the pendants on the dragon robes did not use pearls and jade, preserving a spirit of simplicity; yet when forming the guard of honor they again blazed with banners, glorified embroidered garments, and profaned them with ball-staves—was this not following the habits of Tang and the Five Dynasties, still unable to cast off their vulgarity entirely?
translations.idiomatic: Early Song dragon robes omitted pearl and jade pendants, preserving a spirit of simplicity; yet in forming the guard of honor they again blazed with banners, glorified embroidered garments, and debased ritual with ball-staves—did this not follow Tang and Five Dynasties habits, failing to shed their vulgarity entirely?

sentences.zh: 詒之子孫，殆有甚焉者矣。

translations.literal: What was bequeathed to their descendants was likely something even worse.
translations.idiomatic: What they bequeathed to their descendants was likely worse still.

sentences.zh: 迄於徽宗，奉身之欲，奢蕩靡極，雖欲不亡得乎？

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Huizong, desires for personal indulgence reached extravagant excess without limit—how could the dynasty not perish even if it wished otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Huizong's reign, personal indulgence had reached boundless extravagance—how could the dynasty have survived even if it wished to?

sentences.zh: 靖康之末，累朝法物，淪沒於金。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jingkang era, the ritual objects accumulated over many reigns were lost to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jingkang era, ritual objects accumulated over many reigns were lost to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 中興，掇拾散逸，參酌時宜，務從省約。

translations.literal: After the restoration, they gathered what had been scattered and lost, weighed the needs of the time, and strove for economy.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration they gathered what had been scattered, weighed present needs, and strove for economy.

sentences.zh: 凡服用錦繡，皆易以纈、以羅；

translations.literal: All garments that had used brocade and embroidery were changed to patterned silk and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: All garments that had used brocade and embroidery were replaced with patterned silk and gauze.

sentences.zh: 旗仗用金銀飾者，皆易以繪、以髹。

translations.literal: All banners and regalia that had used gold and silver ornament were changed to painted and lacquered work.
translations.idiomatic: All banners and regalia that had used gold and silver ornament were replaced with painted and lacquered work.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，有事郊報，仗內拂扇當用珠飾。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Jianyan era, when there was a suburban sacrifice, the whisk-fans within the guard of honor were to use pearl ornament.
translations.idiomatic: In early Jianyan, when a suburban sacrifice was held, the whisk-fans in the guard of honor were to bear pearl ornament.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：“事天貴質，若尚華麗，非禋祀本意也。”

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "In serving Heaven, simplicity is prized; if one esteems splendor, that is not the original intent of the suburban sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "In serving Heaven, simplicity is prized; to favor splendor is not the true intent of the suburban sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 是以子孫世守其訓，雖江介一隅，而華質適時，尚足為一代之法。

translations.literal: Therefore their descendants guarded this teaching through the generations; although they held only a corner of the land south of the Yangzi, their balance of ornament and substance suited the times and was still sufficient to serve as the law of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Their descendants therefore guarded this teaching through the generations; though they held only a corner south of the Yangzi, their balance of ornament and substance suited the times and sufficed as the standard of an age.

sentences.zh: 其儒臣名物度數之學，見諸論議，又有可觀者焉。

translations.literal: Their Confucian ministers' learning in the names of things and in measures and numbers, as seen in their discussions, also had points worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: Their Confucian ministers' scholarship on ritual names, measures, and numbers, as seen in court debates, also had much worth noting.

sentences.zh: 今取舊史所載，著於篇，作《輿服志》。

translations.literal: Now taking what the old histories record, I set it down in these chapters and compose the Treatise on Carriages and Clothes.
translations.idiomatic: I now take what the old histories record, set it down in these chapters, and compose the Treatise on Carriages and Clothes.

sentences.zh: 五輅。

translations.literal: The Five Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 宋自神宗以降，銳意稽古，禮文之事，招延儒士，折衷同異。

translations.literal: From Emperor Shenzong of Song onward, the court keenly investigated antiquity; in matters of ritual texts it summoned Confucian scholars and reconciled divergent views.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Shenzong onward the court keenly investigated antiquity, summoned Confucian scholars on ritual matters, and reconciled divergent views.

sentences.zh: 元豐有詳定禮文所，徽宗大觀間有議禮局，政和又有禮製局。

translations.literal: Under the Yuanfeng era there was the Office for the Detailed Determination of Ritual Texts; under Emperor Huizong in the Daguang period there was the Bureau for Discussing Ritual; under the Zhenghe era there was again the Bureau for Ritual Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanfeng era had the Office for the Detailed Determination of Ritual Texts; under Huizong in the Daguang period there was the Bureau for Discussing Ritual; and under Zhenghe there was the Bureau for Ritual Regulations.

sentences.zh: 先是，元豐雖置局造輅，而五輅及副輅，多仍唐舊。

translations.literal: Earlier, although Yuanfeng had established a bureau to make carriages, the five imperial carriages and their secondary carriages largely followed Tang practice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, although Yuanfeng had established a bureau to make carriages, the five imperial carriages and their secondary carriages largely followed Tang models.

sentences.zh: 玉輅，自唐顯慶中傳之，至宋曰顯慶輅，親郊則乘之。

translations.literal: The jade carriage was handed down from the Xianqing era of Tang; in Song it was called the Xianqing carriage, and the emperor rode it when personally performing the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The jade carriage had been handed down since Tang's Xianqing era; in Song it was called the Xianqing carriage, and the emperor rode it when personally performing the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 製作精巧，行止安重，後載太常與闟戟，分左右以均輕重，世之良工，莫能為之。

translations.literal: Its construction was exquisitely fine; in motion and at rest it was steady and weighty. Behind it were carried the Grand Standard and the halberd of honor, placed left and right to balance the weight—no master craftsman of the age could make it.
translations.idiomatic: Its craftsmanship was exquisite and it moved with steady, weighty grace. The Grand Standard and the halberd of honor were carried behind, placed left and right to balance its weight—no master craftsman of the age could replicate it.

sentences.zh: 其製：箱上置平盤、黃屋，四柱皆油畫刻鏤。

translations.literal: Its construction: upon the box were set a level platform and a yellow canopy; the four pillars were all painted in oil colors and carved in openwork.
translations.idiomatic: Its design placed a level platform and yellow canopy atop the box; all four pillars were painted in oil colors and carved in openwork.

sentences.zh: 左青龍，右白虎，龜文，金鳳翅，雜花，龍鳳，金塗銀裝，間以玉飾。

translations.literal: On the left the azure dragon, on the right the white tiger, tortoise patterns, golden phoenix wings, mixed flowers, dragons and phoenixes, fittings of gold over silver, interspersed with jade ornament.
translations.idiomatic: On the left stood the azure dragon, on the right the white tiger, with tortoise patterns, golden phoenix wings, mixed floral designs, dragons and phoenixes, gold-over-silver fittings, and jade ornament interspersed throughout.

sentences.zh: 頂輪三層，外施銀耀葉，輪衣、小帶、絡帶並青羅繡雲龍，周綴糸畏帶、羅文佩、銀穗球、小鈴。

translations.literal: The crown wheel had three layers; on the outside were affixed silver radiating leaves; the wheel cover, small bands, and net bands were all of azure silk embroidered with cloud-dragons; around them were hung silk awe-bands, silk-pattern pendants, silver tassel balls, and small bells.
translations.idiomatic: The crown wheel had three tiers with silver radiating leaves on the outside; wheel covers, narrow bands, and net bands were all of azure silk embroidered with cloud-dragons, hung round with silk awe-bands, patterned silk pendants, silver tassel balls, and small bells.

sentences.zh: 平盤上布黃褥，四角勾闌設圓鑒、翟羽。

translations.literal: On the level platform was spread a yellow mat; at the four corners of the hooked railing were set round mirrors and pheasant feathers.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow mat was spread on the level platform; at the four corners of the hooked railing stood round mirrors and pheasant feathers.

sentences.zh: 虛匱內貼銀鏤香罨，軾匱銀龍二，銜香囊，銀香爐，香寶，錦帶，下有障塵。

translations.literal: Within the hollow case was affixed a silver openwork incense holder; on the rail case were two silver dragons holding incense pouches, a silver incense burner, incense jewels, brocade bands, and below a dust screen.
translations.idiomatic: Within the hollow case was affixed a silver openwork incense holder; on the rail case two silver dragons held incense pouches, with a silver incense burner, incense jewels, brocade bands, and a dust screen below.

sentences.zh: 青畫輪轅，銀轂乘葉，三轅，銀龍頭，橫木上有銀鳳十二。

translations.literal: The wheel hubs and shafts were painted azure; the hub caps had silver leaf ornament; there were three shafts with silver dragon heads; on the crossbeam were twelve silver phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Wheel hubs and shafts were painted azure; hub caps bore silver leaf ornament; three shafts bore silver dragon heads; and twelve silver phoenixes stood on the crossbeam.

sentences.zh: 左建青旗，十有二旒，皆繡升龍；

translations.literal: On the left was raised an azure banner with twelve tassels, all embroidered with ascending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: On the left rose an azure banner with twelve tassels, all embroidered with ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 右載闟戟，繡黻文，並青繡綢杠。

translations.literal: On the right was carried the halberd of honor embroidered with fu patterns, both on azure embroidered silk poles.
translations.idiomatic: On the right was carried the halberd of honor embroidered with fu patterns, both on azure embroidered silk poles.

sentences.zh: 又設青繡門簾，銀飾梯一，拓叉二，推竿一，銀錔頭，銀裝行馬，青繒裹免索。

translations.literal: There were also set an azure embroidered door curtain, one silver-ornamented ladder, two support forks, one pushing pole, silver cap ends, silver-fitted traveling horses, and azure silk wrapping the leading ropes.
translations.idiomatic: There were also an azure embroidered door curtain, one silver-ornamented ladder, two support forks, one pushing pole, silver cap ends, silver-fitted traveling horses, and azure silk wrapping the leading ropes.

sentences.zh: 駕六青馬，馬有金麵，插雕羽，鞶纓，攀胸鈴拂，青繡屜，錦包尾。

translations.literal: It was drawn by six azure horses; the horses had golden face plates, inserted carved feathers, breast straps and tassels, chest bells and whiskers, azure embroidered trappings, and brocade-wrapped tails.
translations.idiomatic: Six azure horses drew it, each with a golden face plate, carved feather plumes, breast straps and tassels, chest bells and whiskers, azure embroidered trappings, and brocade-wrapped tails.

sentences.zh: 又誕馬二，在輅前，飾同駕馬。

translations.literal: There were also two lead horses before the carriage, ornamented like the drawing horses.
translations.idiomatic: Two lead horses walked before the carriage, ornamented like the team horses.

sentences.zh: 〈（餘輅及副輅皆有之。）〉

translations.literal: (The remaining carriages and the secondary carriages all had these as well.)
translations.idiomatic: (The remaining imperial carriages and the secondary carriages all had these as well.)

sentences.zh: 駕士六十四人。

translations.literal: Sixty-four carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-four carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 金輅色以赤，駕六赤馬，建大旂，駕士六十四人。

translations.literal: The metal carriage was colored red; it was drawn by six red horses and bore the great banner; sixty-four carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The metal carriage was red; six red horses drew it and it bore the great banner, with sixty-four attendants.

sentences.zh: 象輅色以淺黃，駕六赭白馬，建大赤，駕士四十人。

translations.literal: The ivory carriage was colored pale yellow; it was drawn by six sorrel-white horses and bore the great red banner; forty carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The ivory carriage was pale yellow; six sorrel-white horses drew it and it bore the great red banner, with forty attendants.

sentences.zh: 革輅色以黃，駕六騧馬，建大白，駕士四十人。

translations.literal: The leather carriage was colored yellow; it was drawn by six piebald horses and bore the great white banner; forty carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The leather carriage was yellow; six piebald horses drew it and it bore the great white banner, with forty attendants.

sentences.zh: 木輅色以黑，駕六黑騮馬，建大麾，駕士四十人。

translations.literal: The wood carriage was colored black; it was drawn by six black bay horses and bore the great standard; forty carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The wood carriage was black; six black bay horses drew it and it bore the great standard, with forty attendants.

sentences.zh: 自金輅而下，其製皆同玉輅，惟無玉飾。

translations.literal: From the metal carriage downward, the construction was all the same as the jade carriage, except without jade ornament.
translations.idiomatic: From the metal carriage downward, construction matched the jade carriage except for the absence of jade ornament.

sentences.zh: 五副輅並駕六馬，駕士四十人，當用銀飾者，皆以銅，餘製如正輅。

translations.literal: The five secondary carriages were each drawn by six horses with forty attendants; where silver ornament should have been used, copper was used instead; the rest of the construction was like the principal carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five secondary carriages was drawn by six horses with forty attendants; silver ornament was replaced with copper, but otherwise construction matched the principal carriages.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，議禮局更上皇帝車輅之製，詔頒行。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, the Bureau for Discussing Ritual again submitted regulations for the emperor's carriages, and an edict ordered their promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenghe the Bureau for Discussing Ritual submitted revised regulations for the emperor's carriages, and an edict ordered their promulgation.

sentences.zh: 玉輅，箱上平盤、黃屋以下皆如舊。

translations.literal: The jade carriage: from the level platform and yellow canopy atop the box downward, all was as before.
translations.idiomatic: For the jade carriage, from the level platform and yellow canopy atop the box downward, all remained as before.

sentences.zh: 頂輪三層，內一層素，輪頂上施金塗銀山花葉及翟羽，青絲繡雲龍絡帶二，周綴雜色糸畏帶八、銅佩八、銀穗球二。

translations.literal: The crown wheel had three layers; the inner layer was plain; on the wheel top were affixed gold-over-silver mountain-flower leaves and pheasant feathers; two azure silk cloud-dragon net bands; around them eight multicolored silk awe-bands, eight copper pendants, and two silver tassel balls.
translations.idiomatic: The crown wheel had three tiers, the inner plain; atop it stood gold-over-silver mountain-flower leaves and pheasant feathers, two azure silk cloud-dragon net bands, and around them eight multicolored silk awe-bands, eight copper pendants, and two silver tassel balls.

sentences.zh: 平盤上布紅羅繡雲龍褥，曲幾、扶幾，上下設銀螭首二十四。

translations.literal: On the level platform was spread a red silk mat embroidered with cloud-dragons; curved armrests and supporting armrests; above and below were set twenty-four silver chi-dragon heads.
translations.idiomatic: A red silk mat embroidered with cloud-dragons was spread on the level platform, with curved and supporting armrests and twenty-four silver chi-dragon heads set above and below.

sentences.zh: 四角勾闌設圓鑒一十六，青羅繡寶相花帶，火珠二十八。

translations.literal: At the four corners of the hooked railing were set sixteen round mirrors; azure silk embroidered treasure-flower bands; twenty-eight fire pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen round mirrors stood at the four corners of the hooked railing, with azure silk treasure-flower bands and twenty-eight fire pearls.

sentences.zh: 香匱設香爐，紅羅繡寶相花帶香囊，香寶，銀結綬二，紅羅繡雲龍結綬一，紅錦幟龍鳳門簾一。

translations.literal: The incense case held an incense burner; red silk embroidered treasure-flower-band incense pouches; incense jewels; two silver knot-cords; one red silk cloud-dragon knot-cord; one red brocade dragon-and-phoenix door curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The incense case held a burner, red silk treasure-flower incense pouches, incense jewels, two silver knot-cords, one red silk cloud-dragon knot-cord, and one red brocade dragon-and-phoenix door curtain.

sentences.zh: 青畫輪轅，銀轂乘葉。

translations.literal: The wheel hubs and shafts were painted azure; the hub caps had silver leaf ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Wheel hubs and shafts were painted azure, with silver leaf ornament on the hub caps.

sentences.zh: 軾匱、橫轅、前轅並飾以金塗銀螭首，橫轅上施銀立鳳一十二。

translations.literal: The rail case, cross shaft, and front shaft were all ornamented with gold-over-silver chi-dragon heads; on the cross shaft were set twelve standing silver phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: The rail case, cross shaft, and front shaft were ornamented with gold-over-silver chi-dragon heads, and twelve standing silver phoenixes were set on the cross shaft.

sentences.zh: 左建太常，十有二旒；

translations.literal: On the left was raised the Grand Standard with twelve tassels.
translations.idiomatic: On the left rose the Grand Standard with twelve tassels.

sentences.zh: 右載闟戟，繡黻文。

translations.literal: On the right was carried the halberd of honor embroidered with fu patterns.
translations.idiomatic: On the right was carried the halberd of honor embroidered with fu patterns.

sentences.zh: 杠絝一，以青繡，杠首飾以銀螭首。

translations.literal: One pole wrapping of azure embroidery; the pole head was ornamented with a silver chi-dragon head.
translations.idiomatic: One pole was wrapped in azure embroidery, its head ornamented with a silver chi-dragon.

sentences.zh: 金塗銅鈸，青犛牛尾拂，青繒裹索。

translations.literal: Gold-over-copper cymbals; an azure yak-tail whisk; azure silk wrapping the ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-over-copper cymbals, an azure yak-tail whisk, and azure silk wrapping the ropes.

sentences.zh: 駕青馬六，馬有銅麵，插雕羽，鞶纓，攀胸鈴拂，青線織屜，紅錦包尾。

translations.literal: Drawn by six azure horses; the horses had copper face plates, inserted carved feathers, breast straps and tassels, chest bells and whiskers, azure thread-woven trappings, and red brocade-wrapped tails.
translations.idiomatic: Six azure horses drew it, each with a copper face plate, carved feather plumes, breast straps and tassels, chest bells and whiskers, azure thread-woven trappings, and red brocade-wrapped tails.

sentences.zh: 又踏路馬二，在輅前，飾同駕馬。

translations.literal: There were also two path-treading horses before the carriage, ornamented like the drawing horses.
translations.idiomatic: Two path-treading horses walked before the carriage, ornamented like the team horses.

sentences.zh: 凡大祭祀乘之。

translations.literal: It was ridden for all great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode it for all major sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 金輅以下，並以次列其後。

translations.literal: The metal carriage and those below were all arrayed in order behind it.
translations.idiomatic: The metal carriage and those below were arrayed in order behind it.

sentences.zh: 若大朝會、冊命皇太子諸王大臣，則設五輅於大慶殿庭，為充庭之儀。

translations.literal: If there was a great court assembly or an investiture of the crown prince, princes, or great ministers, the five carriages were set up in the court of the Hall of Great Celebration as the ceremony of filling the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: At great court assemblies or investitures of the crown prince, princes, or great ministers, the five carriages were set up in the court of the Hall of Great Celebration as the ceremony of filling the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 金輅赤質，以金飾諸末，建大旂，餘同玉輅，駕赤馬六；

translations.literal: The metal carriage was of red substance, with gold ornament on all extremities; it bore the great banner; the rest was like the jade carriage; drawn by six red horses.
translations.idiomatic: The metal carriage was red in substance with gold ornament on all extremities; it bore the great banner; otherwise it matched the jade carriage and was drawn by six red horses.

sentences.zh: 凡玉輅之飾以青者，金輅以緋。

translations.literal: Wherever the jade carriage used azure ornament, the metal carriage used scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Where the jade carriage used azure ornament, the metal carriage used scarlet.

sentences.zh: 象輅淺黃質，金塗銅裝，以象飾諸末，建大赤，餘同玉輅，駕赭白馬六；

translations.literal: The ivory carriage was of pale yellow substance, with gold-over-copper fittings, ivory ornament on all extremities; it bore the great red banner; the rest was like the jade carriage; drawn by six sorrel-white horses.
translations.idiomatic: The ivory carriage was pale yellow with gold-over-copper fittings and ivory ornament on all extremities; it bore the great red banner; otherwise it matched the jade carriage and was drawn by six sorrel-white horses.

sentences.zh: 凡玉輅之飾以青者，象輅以銀褐。

translations.literal: Wherever the jade carriage used azure ornament, the ivory carriage used silver-brown.
translations.idiomatic: Where the jade carriage used azure ornament, the ivory carriage used silver-brown.

sentences.zh: 革輅黃質，鞔之以革，建大白，餘同玉輅，駕騧馬六；

translations.literal: The leather carriage was of yellow substance, covered with leather; it bore the great white banner; the rest was like the jade carriage; drawn by six piebald horses.
translations.idiomatic: The leather carriage was yellow and covered with leather; it bore the great white banner; otherwise it matched the jade carriage and was drawn by six piebald horses.

sentences.zh: 凡玉輅之飾以青者，革輅以黃。

translations.literal: Wherever the jade carriage used azure ornament, the leather carriage used yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Where the jade carriage used azure ornament, the leather carriage used yellow.

sentences.zh: 木輅黑質漆之，建大麾，餘同玉輅，駕黑騮六；

translations.literal: The wood carriage was of black substance lacquered; it bore the great standard; the rest was like the jade carriage; drawn by six black bay horses.
translations.idiomatic: The wood carriage was black and lacquered; it bore the great standard; otherwise it matched the jade carriage and was drawn by six black bay horses.

sentences.zh: 凡玉輅之飾以青者，木輅以皂。

translations.literal: Wherever the jade carriage used azure ornament, the wood carriage used black.
translations.idiomatic: Where the jade carriage used azure ornament, the wood carriage used black.

sentences.zh: 凡玉輅用金塗銀裝者，象輅、革輅、木輅及五副輅，並金塗銅裝。

translations.literal: Wherever the jade carriage used gold-over-silver fittings, the ivory, leather, and wood carriages and the five secondary carriages all used gold-over-copper fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Where the jade carriage used gold-over-silver fittings, the ivory, leather, and wood carriages and all five secondary carriages used gold-over-copper fittings instead.

sentences.zh: 又禮製局言：“玉輅馬纓十二而無采，不應古製，欲以五采罽飾樊纓十有二就。

translations.literal: The Bureau for Ritual Regulations also said: "The jade carriage's horse tassels are twelve in number but without colors, which does not accord with ancient institutions; we wish to ornament the bridle tassels with twelve sets of five-colored felt."
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau for Ritual Regulations also reported, "The jade carriage's twelve horse tassels lack color, which does not accord with ancient practice; we propose ornamenting the bridle tassels with twelve sets of five-colored felt."

sentences.zh: 輅衡、軾並無鸞和，乞添置。

translations.literal: The carriage crossbar and rail have neither luan-bird ornaments nor harmony bells; we request that these be added.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage crossbar and rail lack luan-bird ornaments and harmony bells; we request that these be added.

sentences.zh: 蓋弓二十有二，不應古製，乞增為二十八，以象星。

translations.literal: The canopy ribs are twenty-two in number, which does not accord with ancient institutions; we request that they be increased to twenty-eight to symbolize the stars.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy has twenty-two ribs, which does not accord with ancient practice; we request increasing them to twenty-eight to symbolize the stars.

sentences.zh: 又《巾車》言‘玉輅建太常’而不言色，《司常》注云：‘九旗之帛皆用絳，以周尚赤故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Director of Carriages says that "the jade carriage raises the Grand Standard" but does not specify the color; the commentary on the Director of Banners says: "The silk of the nine banners all used scarlet, because Zhou esteemed red."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Director of Carriages says the jade carriage "raises the Grand Standard" but does not specify its color; the commentary on the Director of Banners notes, "The silk of the nine banners all used scarlet, because Zhou esteemed red."

sentences.zh: ’《禮記·月令》中央‘天子乘大輅，載黃旂’，以金、象、木、革四輅及所建之旂，與四時所乘所載皆合。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances in the Book of Rites says that at the center "the Son of Heaven rides the great carriage and bears the yellow banner"; the metal, ivory, wood, and leather carriages and the banners they raise all accord with what is ridden and borne in the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances in the Book of Rites states that at the center "the Son of Heaven rides the great carriage and bears the yellow banner"; the metal, ivory, wood, and leather carriages and their banners all accord with what is ridden and borne in the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 今玉輅所建之旂，以青帛十二幅連屬為之，有升龍而非交龍，又無三辰，皆非古製。

translations.literal: The banner now raised on the jade carriage is made of twelve panels of azure silk joined together; it has ascending dragons rather than interlaced dragons, and lacks the three luminaries—all of which are not ancient institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The banner now raised on the jade carriage is made of twelve joined panels of azure silk; it bears ascending dragons rather than interlaced dragons and lacks the sun, moon, and stars—all departures from ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 如依成周以所尚之色則用赤，依《月令》兼四代之製則當用黃，仍分縿、斿之製及繡畫三辰於其上。

translations.literal: If one follows completed Zhou according to the color it esteemed, scarlet should be used; if one follows the Monthly Ordinances combining the institutions of the four ages, yellow should be used; still dividing the lower and upper fringe forms and embroidering the three luminaries upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Following completed Zhou and its favored color, scarlet should be used; following the Monthly Ordinances and the combined institutions of the four ages, yellow should be used—with proper lower and upper fringe forms and the three luminaries embroidered upon it.

sentences.zh: 今改製，太常其斿曳地，當依《周官》以六人維之。

translations.literal: In the present revised regulations, the Grand Standard's fringe trails on the ground; according to the Rites of Zhou six men should hold it in place.
translations.idiomatic: Under the revised regulations, the Grand Standard's fringe trails on the ground; according to the Rites of Zhou six men should steady it.

sentences.zh: 又《左傳》言：‘、鸞、和、鈴，昭其聲也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Zhuan also says: "Banners, luan-bird ornaments, harmony bells, and ringing bells proclaim their sound."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Zhuan also says, "Banners, luan-bird ornaments, harmony bells, and ringing bells proclaim their sound."

sentences.zh: ’注：‘錫在馬額，鈴在旂首。

translations.literal: The commentary says: "The xi ornament is on the horse's forehead; the bell is at the banner head."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains, "The xi ornament is on the horse's forehead; the bell is at the banner head."

sentences.zh: ’今旂首無鈴，乞增置。

translations.literal: Now the banner head has no bell; we request that one be added.
translations.idiomatic: The banner head now lacks a bell; we request that one be added.

sentences.zh: 又車蓋周以流蘇及佩各八，無所法象，欲各增為十二，以應天數。

translations.literal: Moreover, around the carriage canopy the tassels and pendants are each eight in number, symbolizing nothing; we wish to increase each to twelve to correspond to the number of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the tassels and pendants around the carriage canopy are each eight in number, symbolizing nothing; we propose increasing each to twelve to correspond to the number of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又輅之諸末，盡飾以玉，為稱其實，而羅紋雜佩乃用塗金，乞改為玉。

translations.literal: Moreover, on all the terminal fittings of the carriage they are entirely decorated with jade, to match its substance, yet the luo-pattern mixed pendants use gold plating; we request they be changed to jade.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, all the terminal fittings of the carriage are decorated with jade to match its substance, yet the luo-pattern mixed pendants are gold-plated; we request that these be changed to jade as well.

sentences.zh: 又車箱兩轓有金塗龜文及鶤翅，左龍右虎，乃後代之製，欲改用蟉龍，加玉為飾。”

translations.literal: Moreover, on both side panels of the carriage box there are gold-plated tortoise patterns and kun-bird wings, with a dragon on the left and a tiger on the right—these are institutions of later ages; we wish to change them to curling dragons and add jade as ornament."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, both side panels of the carriage box bear gold-plated tortoise patterns and kun-bird wings, with a dragon on the left and a tiger on the right—features of later ages. We propose replacing them with curling dragons and adding jade ornament.

sentences.zh: 又言：“既建太常當車之後，則自後登車有妨。

translations.literal: He further said: "Since the Grand Standard is erected behind the center of the carriage, boarding from the rear would be obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: He further said, "Since the Grand Standard is erected directly behind the carriage, boarding from the rear would be obstructed.

sentences.zh: 《曲禮》言：‘君車將駕，則仆執策立於馬前，已駕，仆展令，效駕，奮衣由右上，取貳綏跪乘，執策分轡，驅之，五步而立，君出就車。

translations.literal: The Classic of Rites (Qu Li) says: 'When the ruler's carriage is about to be harnessed, the attendant holds the whip and stands before the horses. Once harnessed, the attendant spreads the command, tests the harness, lifts his robe and mounts from the right side, takes the secondary hand-rope and kneels to ride, holds the whip and separates the reins, drives the horses, then stands still after five paces while the ruler comes out and enters the carriage.'
translations.idiomatic: The Qu Li says, "When the ruler's carriage is about to be harnessed, the attendant holds the whip and stands before the horses. Once the horses are harnessed, the attendant issues the command, tests the harness, lifts his robe and mounts from the right, takes the secondary hand-rope and kneels to ride, holds the whip and separates the reins, drives the horses forward, then halts after five paces while the ruler comes out and enters the carriage."

sentences.zh: ’則君升車亦當自右，由前而入。

translations.literal: ' Thus the ruler in mounting the carriage should also do so from the right, entering from the front.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the ruler, in mounting the carriage, should likewise do so from the right, entering from the front.

sentences.zh: 今玉輅前有式匱，不應古製，恐當更易，以便登車及改式之製。

translations.literal: Now in front of the jade carriage there is a shi compartment, which does not accord with ancient institutions; it probably should be changed to facilitate boarding and revise the shi institution.
translations.idiomatic: The jade carriage now has a shi compartment in front, which does not accord with ancient practice; it should probably be altered to facilitate boarding and to restore the proper shi design.

sentences.zh: 又《禮記》言‘車得其式’，《周官·輿人》：‘三分其隧，一在前，二在後，以揉其式，以其廣之半為之式崇。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites also says 'the carriage obtains its shi,' and the Rites of Zhou, Director of Carriage Makers: 'Divide the depth into three parts—one in front and two in back—to shape the shi, and make the height of the shi half its width.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites also states that "the carriage obtains its shi," and the Rites of Zhou's Director of Carriage Makers specifies: "Divide the depth into three parts—one in front and two in back—to shape the shi, and make the height of the shi half its width."

sentences.zh: 三分軫圍，去一以為式圍。

translations.literal: Divide the frame perimeter into three parts and remove one to make the shi perimeter.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the frame perimeter into three parts and subtract one to determine the shi perimeter.

sentences.zh: 三分軹圍，去一以為對圍。

translations.literal: Divide the zhi perimeter into three parts and remove one to make the dui perimeter.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the zhi perimeter into three parts and subtract one to determine the dui perimeter.

sentences.zh: ’注：‘立者為對，橫者為軹。

translations.literal: ' The commentary: 'The upright piece is the dui; the horizontal piece is the zhi.'
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains, "The upright piece is the dui; the horizontal piece is the zhi."

sentences.zh: ’今玉輅無式。”

translations.literal: ' Now the jade carriage has no shi.
translations.idiomatic: The jade carriage, however, has no shi at all.

sentences.zh: 詔：“ 玉輅用青質，輪輈絡帶，其色如之。

translations.literal: An edict: "The jade carriage shall use azure as its substance; the wheel felloes and luo belts shall be of the same color.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "The jade carriage shall be azure in substance, and the wheel felloes and luo belts shall match that color.

sentences.zh: 四柱、平盤、虛匱則用赤，增蓋弓之數為二十八，左右建旂、常，並青。

translations.literal: The four pillars, level platform, and empty compartment shall use scarlet; increase the number of canopy ribs to twenty-eight; erect banners and standards on left and right, all azure.
translations.idiomatic: The four pillars, level platform, and empty compartment shall be scarlet; the number of canopy ribs shall be increased to twenty-eight; banners and standards shall be erected on left and right, all in azure.

sentences.zh: 太常繡日月、五星、二十八宿，旂上則繡以雲龍。

translations.literal: The Grand Standard is embroidered with the sun, moon, five planets, and twenty-eight constellations; on the banner dragons amid clouds are embroidered.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Standard shall be embroidered with the sun, moon, five planets, and twenty-eight constellations; the banner shall bear cloud-dragons in embroidery.

sentences.zh: 朱杠，青縚，鈴垂十有二就，流蘇及佩各增十二之數。

translations.literal: Scarlet crossbars, azure cords; bells hang in twelve sets; tassels and pendants each increased to twelve in number.
translations.idiomatic: Crossbars shall be scarlet and cords azure; bells shall hang in twelve sets; tassels and pendants shall each be increased to twelve.

sentences.zh: 樊纓飾以五采之罽，衡式之上又加鸞和。

translations.literal: The bridle ornaments decorated with five-colored felt; above the crossbar and shi, luan-bird and harmony bells are added.
translations.idiomatic: Bridle ornaments shall be adorned with five-colored felt, and luan-bird and harmony bells shall be added above the crossbar and shi.

sentences.zh: 輅之諸末，耀葉、螭頭、雲龍、垂牙、鎚腳、花版、結綬、羅紋雜佩、羽台、蔥台、麻爐、香寶、壓貼牌字，皆飾以玉。

translations.literal: On all terminal fittings of the carriage—radiating leaves, chitou, cloud-dragons, hanging teeth, hammer feet, flower panels, knotted sashes, luo-pattern mixed pendants, feather platforms, scallion platforms, hemp censers, fragrant treasures, and pressed plaque characters—all are decorated with jade.
translations.idiomatic: All terminal fittings of the carriage—radiating leaves, chitou, cloud-dragons, hanging teeth, hammer feet, flower panels, knotted sashes, luo-pattern mixed pendants, feather platforms, scallion platforms, hemp censers, fragrant treasures, and pressed plaque characters—shall be ornamented with jade.

sentences.zh: 自後而升，式匱不去。

translations.literal: One mounts from the rear; the shi compartment is not removed.
translations.idiomatic: Boarding shall be from the rear, and the shi compartment shall remain in place.

sentences.zh: 既成，高二丈七寸五分，闊一丈五尺。

translations.literal: When completed, it was two zhang, seven cun, and five fen in height, and one zhang and five chi in breadth.
translations.idiomatic: When completed, it stood two zhang, seven cun, and five fen high and one zhang and five chi wide.

sentences.zh: 副玉輅，亦用青色，舊駕馬四，增為六，色亦以青。”

translations.literal: The secondary jade carriage also used azure; formerly four horses drew it, increased to six, their color also azure.
translations.idiomatic: The secondary jade carriage likewise used azure; where four horses had formerly drawn it, the number was increased to six, all azure in color.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，詔改修正副輅，討論製造金、象、革、木四輅，並依新修玉輅制度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered revision of the main and secondary carriages, and discussion of manufacturing the gold, ivory, leather, and wood carriages, all following the newly revised jade carriage regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhenghe reign, an edict ordered the revision of the main and secondary carriages and the manufacture of the gold, ivory, leather, and wood carriages, all according to the newly revised jade carriage regulations.

sentences.zh: 旂、常並建，各與輅一色。

translations.literal: Banners and standards shall both be erected, each matching the color of its carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Banners and standards shall both be erected, each matching the color of its carriage.

sentences.zh: 除去闟戟，改車箱兩轓龜文、鶤翅、左龍、右虎之飾，並用蟉龍。

translations.literal: Remove the gate halberds; change the tortoise patterns, kun wings, left dragon, and right tiger decorations on both side panels of the carriage box, all to curling dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The gate halberds were to be removed, and the tortoise patterns, kun wings, left dragon, and right tiger on both side panels of the carriage box were to be replaced with curling dragons.

sentences.zh: 增蓋弓、博山、流蘇等數，軾衡加和鸞，以合於古。

translations.literal: Increase the numbers of canopy ribs, boushan ornaments, tassels, and the like; add harmony bells and luan ornaments to the crossbar and balance, to accord with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The numbers of canopy ribs, boushan ornaments, tassels, and the like were to be increased, and harmony bells and luan ornaments added to the crossbar and balance, to accord with ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 金輅朱質，飾以金塗銀；

translations.literal: The gold carriage of scarlet substance, decorated with gold-plated silver;
translations.idiomatic: The gold carriage: scarlet in substance, ornamented with gold-plated silver;

sentences.zh: 左右建太常、大旂及輪衣、絡帶等，色皆以黃；

translations.literal: Erect the Grand Standard and great banner left and right, with wheel covers, luo belts, and the like, all in yellow;
translations.idiomatic: On left and right, the Grand Standard and great banner, along with wheel covers and luo belts, all in yellow;

sentences.zh: 龍旂九斿，如《周官》金輅建大旂之製；

translations.literal: Dragon banner with nine fringes, following the Rites of Zhou institution for the gold carriage raising the great banner;
translations.idiomatic: A dragon banner with nine fringes, following the Rites of Zhou institution for the gold carriage bearing the great banner;

sentences.zh: 駕馬以騧，飾樊纓五采九就。

translations.literal: Drawn by piebald horses, bridle ornaments of five colors in nine sets.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by piebald horses, with bridle ornaments of five colors in nine sets.

sentences.zh: 象輅朱質，凡制度、裝綴、名物並同金輅，飾以象及金塗銀銅鍮石；

translations.literal: The ivory carriage of scarlet substance; all regulations, adornments, and named objects the same as the gold carriage, decorated with ivory and gold-plated silver, copper, and brass;
translations.idiomatic: The ivory carriage: scarlet in substance; all regulations, adornments, and named objects the same as the gold carriage, ornamented with ivory and gold-plated silver, copper, and brass;

sentences.zh: 左右建太常、大赤，輪衣、絡帶等，色皆以紅；

translations.literal: Erect the Grand Standard and Great Scarlet left and right, with wheel covers, luo belts, and the like, all in red;
translations.idiomatic: On left and right, the Grand Standard and Great Scarlet, along with wheel covers and luo belts, all in red;

sentences.zh: 大赤繡鳥隼七斿，如《周官》象輅建大赤之製；

translations.literal: Great Scarlet embroidered with birds of prey, seven fringes, following the Rites of Zhou institution for the ivory carriage raising Great Scarlet;
translations.idiomatic: Great Scarlet embroidered with birds of prey and bearing seven fringes, following the Rites of Zhou institution for the ivory carriage bearing Great Scarlet;

sentences.zh: 駕馬以赤，飾樊纓七就。

translations.literal: Drawn by scarlet horses, bridle ornaments of seven sets.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by scarlet horses, with bridle ornaments of seven sets.

sentences.zh: 革輅朱質，凡制度、裝綴、名物並同金輅，飾以金塗銅鍮石；

translations.literal: The leather carriage of scarlet substance; all regulations, adornments, and named objects the same as the gold carriage, decorated with gold-plated copper and brass;
translations.idiomatic: The leather carriage: scarlet in substance; all regulations, adornments, and named objects the same as the gold carriage, ornamented with gold-plated copper and brass;

sentences.zh: 左右建太常、大白及輪衣、絡帶等，色皆以淺黃；

translations.literal: Erect the Grand Standard and Great White left and right, with wheel covers, luo belts, and the like, all in pale yellow;
translations.idiomatic: On left and right, the Grand Standard and Great White, along with wheel covers and luo belts, all in pale yellow;

sentences.zh: 大白繡熊虎六斿，如《周官》革輅建大白之製；

translations.literal: Great White embroidered with bears and tigers, six fringes, following the Rites of Zhou institution for the leather carriage raising Great White;
translations.idiomatic: Great White embroidered with bears and tigers and bearing six fringes, following the Rites of Zhou institution for the leather carriage bearing Great White;

sentences.zh: 駕馬以赭白，飾樊纓五就。

translations.literal: Drawn by reddish-white horses, bridle ornaments of five sets.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by sorrel-white horses, with bridle ornaments of five sets.

sentences.zh: 木輅朱質，凡制度、裝綴、名物皆同金輅，飾以金塗鍮石；

translations.literal: The wood carriage of scarlet substance; all regulations, adornments, and named objects the same as the gold carriage, decorated with gold-plated brass;
translations.idiomatic: The wood carriage: scarlet in substance; all regulations, adornments, and named objects the same as the gold carriage, ornamented with gold-plated brass;

sentences.zh: 左右建太常、大麾及輪衣、絡帶等，色皆以皂；

translations.literal: Erect the Grand Standard and Great Banner left and right, with wheel covers, luo belts, and the like, all in black;
translations.idiomatic: On left and right, the Grand Standard and Great Banner, along with wheel covers and luo belts, all in black;

sentences.zh: 大麾繡龜蛇四斿，如《周官》木輅建大麾之製；

translations.literal: Great Banner embroidered with turtle and serpent, four fringes, following the Rites of Zhou institution for the wood carriage raising the Great Banner;
translations.idiomatic: Great Banner embroidered with turtle and serpent and bearing four fringes, following the Rites of Zhou institution for the wood carriage bearing the Great Banner;

sentences.zh: 駕馬以烏，飾樊纓三就。

translations.literal: Drawn by black horses, bridle ornaments of three sets.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by black horses, with bridle ornaments of three sets.

sentences.zh: 四輅駕馬各六。

translations.literal: Each of the four carriages drawn by six horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the four carriages was drawn by six horses.

sentences.zh: 玉輅駕士六十四人，餘皆四十人。

translations.literal: The jade carriage had sixty-four carriage attendants; the rest each had forty.
translations.idiomatic: The jade carriage had sixty-four carriage attendants; the others each had forty.

sentences.zh: 又禮製局增改雅飾諸輅：舊副玉輅色青，飾以金，改用黃而飾以玉；

translations.literal: The Ritual Regulations Bureau further revised the elegant adornments of the carriages: formerly the secondary jade carriage was azure and decorated with gold; it was changed to yellow and decorated with jade;
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Regulations Bureau further revised the elegant adornments of the carriages: the secondary jade carriage, formerly azure and ornamented with gold, was changed to yellow and ornamented with jade;

sentences.zh: 樊纓如正輅之製；

translations.literal: Bridle ornaments as on the main carriage;
translations.idiomatic: bridle ornaments as on the main carriage;

sentences.zh: 建太常，色黃，飾以組，象日月於縿、星辰於斿，其長曳地。

translations.literal: Erect the Grand Standard, yellow in color, adorned with ribbons, sun and moon on the lower fringe and stars on the upper fringe, its length trailing on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Standard was erected in yellow, adorned with ribbons, with sun and moon on the lower fringe and stars on the upper fringe, its length trailing on the ground.

sentences.zh: 舊金輅改用青，飾以金；

translations.literal: The former gold carriage was changed to azure and decorated with gold;
translations.idiomatic: The gold carriage was changed to azure and ornamented with gold;

sentences.zh: 樊纓以五采罽而九就；

translations.literal: Bridle ornaments of five-colored felt in nine sets;
translations.idiomatic: bridle ornaments of five-colored felt in nine sets;

sentences.zh: 建大旂，色青，飾以組，象交龍於縿、升龍於斿，其長齊軫。

translations.literal: Erect the great banner, azure in color, adorned with ribbons, interlaced dragons on the lower fringe and ascending dragons on the upper fringe, its length even with the frame.
translations.idiomatic: the great banner was erected in azure, adorned with ribbons, with interlaced dragons on the lower fringe and ascending dragons on the upper fringe, its length even with the frame.

sentences.zh: 象輅改用赤，飾以象；

translations.literal: The ivory carriage was changed to scarlet and decorated with ivory;
translations.idiomatic: The ivory carriage was changed to scarlet and ornamented with ivory;

sentences.zh: 樊纓以五采罽而七就；

translations.literal: Bridle ornaments of five-colored felt in seven sets;
translations.idiomatic: bridle ornaments of five-colored felt in seven sets;

sentences.zh: 建大赤，色赤，飾以組，象鳥隼於縿、斿，其長齊較。

translations.literal: Erect Great Scarlet, scarlet in color, adorned with ribbons, birds of prey on the lower and upper fringes, its length even with the yoke end.
translations.idiomatic: Great Scarlet was erected in scarlet, adorned with ribbons, with birds of prey on the lower and upper fringes, its length even with the yoke end.

sentences.zh: 革輅改用白，飾以革；

translations.literal: The leather carriage was changed to white and decorated with leather;
translations.idiomatic: The leather carriage was changed to white and ornamented with leather;

sentences.zh: 龍勒絛纓，建大白，色白，飾以組，象熊虎於縿、斿，其長齊肩。

translations.literal: Dragon bridle with ribbon tassels; erect Great White, white in color, adorned with ribbons, bears and tigers on the lower and upper fringes, its length even with the shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: with a dragon bridle and ribbon tassels; Great White was erected in white, adorned with ribbons, with bears and tigers on the lower and upper fringes, its length even with the shoulder.

sentences.zh: 三輅皆維以縷，削幅為之。

translations.literal: All three carriages held in place with threads, made by trimming the panels.
translations.idiomatic: All three carriages were held in place with threads, the panels trimmed to size.

sentences.zh: 木輅依舊色，而飾以漆，其色黑；

translations.literal: The wood carriage retained its old color but was decorated with lacquer, its color black;
translations.idiomatic: The wood carriage retained its original color but was ornamented with lacquer, in black;

sentences.zh: 前樊鵠纓，建大麾，色黑，飾以組，象龜蛇於縿、斿，其長齊首；

translations.literal: Front bridle with swan ornament; erect the Great Banner, black in color, adorned with ribbons, turtle and serpent on the lower and upper fringes, its length even with the head;
translations.idiomatic: with a front bridle and swan ornament; the Great Banner was erected in black, adorned with ribbons, with turtle and serpent on the lower and upper fringes, its length even with the head;

sentences.zh: 維以縷，充幅為之。

translations.literal: Held with threads, made with full panels.
translations.idiomatic: It was held with threads, the panels left full.

sentences.zh: 又詔玉輅身仍用紅，太常、旂、絡帶等用黃，餘常、旂、絡帶，亦隨其輅色。

translations.literal: Another edict: the jade carriage body still used red; the Grand Standard, banners, luo belts, and the like used yellow; other standards, banners, and luo belts likewise followed the color of their carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict specified that the jade carriage body should remain red, while the Grand Standard, banners, luo belts, and the like should be yellow; other standards, banners, and luo belts should follow the color of their respective carriages.

sentences.zh: 高宗渡江，鹵簿、儀仗悉毀於兵。

translations.literal: When Gaozong crossed the Yangzi, the imperial guard regalia and ceremonial insignia were all destroyed in the warfare.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong crossed the Yangzi, the imperial guard regalia and ceremonial insignia were all destroyed in the warfare.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年，始命工部尚書莫將、戶部侍郎張澄等以天禧、宣和《鹵簿圖》考究制度，及故內侍工匠省記指說，參酌制度。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shaoxing, Mo Jiang, Minister of Works, Zhang Cheng, Vice Minister of Revenue, and others were first ordered to study the regulations using the Tianxi and Xuanhe Illustrations of the Imperial Guard, and to consult with former palace artisans and craftsmen who could recollect and explain, adjusting the regulations accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Shaoxing reign, Mo Jiang, Minister of Works, Zhang Cheng, Vice Minister of Revenue, and others were first ordered to investigate the regulations using the Tianxi and Xuanhe Illustrations of the Imperial Guard, together with the recollections and explanations of former palace artisans and craftsmen, and to adjust the institutions accordingly.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，玉輅成；

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, the jade carriage was completed;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year, the jade carriage was completed;

sentences.zh: 明年，遂作金、象、革、木四輅，副輅不設。

translations.literal: The following year, the gold, ivory, leather, and wood carriages were made; secondary carriages were not established.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the gold, ivory, leather, and wood carriages were made, but secondary carriages were not provided.

sentences.zh: 玉輅之製，青色，飾以玉，通高十九尺，輪高六十三寸，輻徑三十九寸，軸長十五尺三寸。

translations.literal: The jade carriage's design: azure in color, decorated with jade; overall height nineteen chi; wheel height sixty-three cun; spoke diameter thirty-nine cun; axle length fifteen chi three cun.
translations.idiomatic: The jade carriage was azure in color and ornamented with jade. Its overall height was nineteen chi; wheel height, sixty-three cun; spoke diameter, thirty-nine cun; and axle length, fifteen chi and three cun.

sentences.zh: 頂上剡為輪三層，象天圜也。

translations.literal: At the top carved into three layers of wheels, symbolizing the roundness of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the top it was carved into three layers of wheels, symbolizing the roundness of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 外施青玉博山八十一，

translations.literal: Outside applied eighty-one azure jade boushan ornaments,
translations.idiomatic: On the outside were affixed eighty-one azure jade boushan ornaments,

sentences.zh: 〈（一名耀葉。）〉

translations.literal: (Also called radiating leaves.)
translations.idiomatic: (Also called radiating leaves.)

sentences.zh: 鏤以金塗龍文，覆以青羅，曰輪衣。

translations.literal: Carved with gold-plated dragon patterns, covered with azure gauze, called the wheel cover.
translations.idiomatic: Carved with gold-plated dragon patterns and covered with azure gauze, this was called the wheel cover.

sentences.zh: 綴垂玉佩，間以五色垂氂尾，曰流蘇。

translations.literal: Strung with hanging jade pendants, interspersed with five-colored yak-tail tassels, called tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Strung with hanging jade pendants and interspersed with five-colored yak-tail tassels, these were called tassels.

sentences.zh: 〈（一名糸畏帶。

translations.literal: (Also called silk awe-bands.)
translations.idiomatic: (Also called silk awe-bands.)

sentences.zh: 頂四角分垂青羅曰絡帶，表裏繡雲龍。

translations.literal: From the four corners of the top, azure gauze hangs separately, called luo belts, embroidered with cloud-dragons inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: From the four corners of the top, azure gauze hung separately as luo belts, embroidered with cloud-dragons on both sides.

sentences.zh: 遇雨，則油黃繒覆之。

translations.literal: When it rains, oiled yellow silk covers it.
translations.idiomatic: In rain, it was covered with oiled yellow silk.

sentences.zh: 輅之中四柱，象地方也，前柱卷龍。

translations.literal: Within the carriage four pillars symbolize the squareness of earth; the front pillar is a coiled dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Within the carriage, four pillars symbolized the squareness of earth; the front pillar was formed as a coiled dragon.

sentences.zh: 平盤上布錦褥，前有橫軾，後垂錦軟簾。

translations.literal: On the level platform spread brocade cushions; in front a horizontal crossbar; behind hangs a brocade soft curtain.
translations.idiomatic: On the level platform lay brocade cushions; in front was a horizontal crossbar, and behind hung a brocade soft curtain.

sentences.zh: 登車則自後卷簾梯級以登。

translations.literal: To board, one rolls up the curtain from the rear and ascends by steps.
translations.idiomatic: To board, one rolled up the curtain from the rear and ascended by steps.

sentences.zh: 四面周以闌而闕其中，以備登降。

translations.literal: On all four sides railings encircle it with openings in the center, to provide for ascending and descending.
translations.idiomatic: On all four sides railings encircled it with openings at the center to allow ascent and descent.

sentences.zh: 執綏官先自右升，立於右柱下，以備顧問。

translations.literal: The hand-rope attendant first mounts from the right, stands below the right pillar, to be ready for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: The hand-rope attendant mounted first from the right and stood below the right pillar, ready to assist as needed.

sentences.zh: 闌柱頭有玉蹲龍。

translations.literal: On the railing pillar tops are jade crouching dragons.
translations.idiomatic: On the tops of the railing pillars stood jade crouching dragons.

sentences.zh: 軾前有牌，鏤曰“玉輅”，以玉篆之，上有玉龍二。

translations.literal: Before the crossbar is a plaque engraved "Jade Carriage," written in jade seal script, with two jade dragons above.
translations.idiomatic: Before the crossbar was a plaque engraved with the characters "Jade Carriage" in jade seal script, with two jade dragons above.

sentences.zh: 中設御坐，純以黃香木為之，取其黃中之正色也。

translations.literal: Within is set the imperial seat, made entirely of yellow fragrant wood, taking its proper color from the yellow within.
translations.idiomatic: Within was set the imperial seat, made entirely of yellow fragrant wood, chosen for the proper color at the center of yellow.

sentences.zh: 下有塗金蹲龍十六。

translations.literal: Below are sixteen gold-plated crouching dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Below stood sixteen gold-plated crouching dragons.

sentences.zh: 在平槃四圍下，又有拓角雲龍，金彩飾之，前後左右各二。

translations.literal: Below the four sides of the level platform are also horn-spreading cloud-dragons, decorated in gold, two each front, back, left, and right.
translations.idiomatic: Below the four sides of the level platform were horn-spreading cloud-dragons ornamented in gold, two each to the front, back, left, and right.

sentences.zh: 前有轅木三，鱗體昂首龍形。

translations.literal: In front are three yoke timbers, scaly bodies with raised heads in dragon form.
translations.idiomatic: In front were three yoke timbers, scaly-bodied and dragon-headed with raised snouts.

sentences.zh: 轅木上束兩橫竿，在前者名曰鳳轅，馬負之以行；

translations.literal: On the yoke timbers bound are two horizontal poles; the front one called the phoenix yoke, borne by the horses for movement;
translations.idiomatic: Bound to the yoke timbers were two horizontal poles; the front one, called the phoenix yoke, was borne by the horses to draw the carriage;

sentences.zh: 次曰推轅，班直推之以助馬力。

translations.literal: The next called the pushing yoke, pushed straight by attendants to assist the horses.
translations.idiomatic: the next, called the pushing yoke, was pushed straight by attendants to assist the horses.

sentences.zh: 橫於轅後者名曰壓轅，以人壓於後，欲取其平。

translations.literal: That laid crosswise behind the yoke is called the pressing yoke; men press down from behind, intending to keep it level.
translations.idiomatic: That laid crosswise behind the yoke was called the pressing yoke; men pressed down from behind to keep the carriage level.

sentences.zh: 車輪三歲一易，心用榆，圜數尺，圈以鐵，以防折裂。

translations.literal: Carriage wheels replaced every three years; the hub of elm, round several chi, ringed with iron to prevent splitting.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage wheels were replaced every three years; the hub was of elm, round and several chi across, ringed with iron to prevent splitting.

sentences.zh: 橫貫大木以為軸，夾以兩輪，輪皆彩畫，此輅下飾也。

translations.literal: A great timber runs horizontally as the axle, flanked by two wheels; the wheels all color-painted—this is the ornamentation beneath the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: A great timber ran horizontally as the axle, flanked by two wheels; the wheels were all painted in colors—this was the ornamentation beneath the carriage.

sentences.zh: 每新輪成，載鐵萬斤試之。

translations.literal: Whenever a new wheel was completed, it was tested bearing ten thousand jin of iron.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a new wheel was completed, it was tested by loading it with ten thousand jin of iron.

sentences.zh: 左建太常，右建龍旂，插於輅後兩柱之金環前。

translations.literal: On the left the Grand Standard is erected, on the right the dragon banner, inserted before the gold rings on the two rear pillars of the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On the left the Grand Standard was erected and on the right the dragon banner, inserted before the gold rings on the two rear pillars of the carriage.

sentences.zh: 駕青馬六，馬有鏤錫，鞶纓，金鈴，紅旄繡屜，金包騣，錦包尾，青繒裹索引之。

translations.literal: Six azure horses draw it; the horses have engraved xi ornaments, pan-ying bridles, gold bells, red plume embroidered shoes, gold-wrapped forelocks, brocade-wrapped tails, led with azure silk wrapping the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Six azure horses drew it, each with engraved xi ornaments, pan-ying bridles, gold bells, red-plume embroidered shoes, gold-wrapped forelocks, brocade-wrapped tails, and reins wrapped in azure silk for leading.

sentences.zh: 駕士二百三十二人。

translations.literal: Carriage attendants two hundred thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: There were two hundred thirty-two carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 〈（誕馬十二人，左右索百二十八人，入轅馬十二人，龍頭子二人，前後抱轅各六人，推竿四人，捧輪四人，拓叉四人，淨席四人，前攔人員一人，後攔人員一人，前攔馬八人，後攔馬八人，踏道人員二人，踏道二十人，小拓叉四人，小梯子二人，燭台二人，香匙剪子二人，左右索人員二人。

translations.literal: (Twelve horse handlers; one hundred twenty-eight left and right rope handlers; twelve horses entering the yoke; two dragon-head attendants; six front and six rear yoke-holders; four pole-pushers; four wheel-bearers; four spreading-fork attendants; four mat-cleaners; one front blocking officer; one rear blocking officer; eight front blocking horses; eight rear blocking horses; two path-preparing officers; twenty path-preparers; four small spreading-forks; two small ladders; two candle stands; two incense spoon and scissors attendants; two left-right rope officers.
translations.idiomatic: (Twelve horse handlers; one hundred twenty-eight left and right rope handlers; twelve horses entering the yoke; two dragon-head attendants; six front and six rear yoke-holders; four pole-pushers; four wheel-bearers; four spreading-fork attendants; four mat-cleaners; one front blocking officer; one rear blocking officer; eight front blocking horses; eight rear blocking horses; two path-preparing officers; twenty path-preparers; four small spreading-forks; two small ladders; two candle stands; two attendants for incense spoon and scissors; and two left-right rope officers.

sentences.zh: 鵩又有嗬喝人員二人，教馬官二人，捧輪將軍四人，千牛衛將軍二人，推輪軸官健八人，抱太常龍旗官六人，職掌五人，專知官一人，手分一人，庫子八人，裝掛工匠二人，諸作工匠十五人，蓋覆儀鸞司十一人，監官三員。）〉

translations.literal: Furthermore there were also two shouting officers; two horse-training officials; four wheel-bearing generals; two Thousand-Ox Guard generals; eight wheel-axle pushing guard soldiers; six Grand Standard and dragon banner holders; five duty officers; one specialist officer; one sub-clerk; eight storekeepers; two mounting craftsmen; fifteen workshop craftsmen; eleven canopy-covering Ceremonial Guard personnel; three supervising officers.)
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore there were also two shouting officers; two horse-training officials; four wheel-bearing generals; two Thousand-Ox Guard generals; eight wheel-axle pushing guard soldiers; six Grand Standard and dragon banner holders; five duty officers; one specialist officer; one sub-clerk; eight storekeepers; two mounting craftsmen; fifteen workshop craftsmen; eleven Ceremonial Guard personnel for canopy covering; and three supervising officers.)

sentences.zh: 金輅黃色，飾以金塗銀，製如玉輅，而高減五寸；

translations.literal: The gold carriage yellow in color, decorated with gold-plated silver, its design like the jade carriage but five cun less in height;
translations.idiomatic: The gold carriage was yellow in color and ornamented with gold-plated silver. Its design matched the jade carriage but was five cun lower in height;

sentences.zh: 博山、輪衣、絡帶、轅輻、軸並以黃，建大旂九斿；

translations.literal: Boushan ornaments, wheel covers, luo belts, yoke spokes, and axle all yellow; raises the great banner with nine fringes;
translations.idiomatic: its boushan ornaments, wheel covers, luo belts, yoke spokes, and axle were all yellow, and it bore the great banner with nine fringes;

sentences.zh: 駕黃馬六，駕士一百五十四人。

translations.literal: Drawn by six yellow horses; carriage attendants one hundred fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Six yellow horses drew it, with one hundred fifty-four carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 象輅朱色，飾以象及金塗銅，製如金輅；

translations.literal: The ivory carriage scarlet in color, decorated with ivory and gold-plated copper, its design like the gold carriage;
translations.idiomatic: The ivory carriage was scarlet, ornamented with ivory and gold-plated copper in the same design as the gold carriage;

sentences.zh: 博山、輪衣、絡帶並以朱，建大赤七斿；

translations.literal: Boushan ornaments, wheel covers, and luo belts all scarlet; raises the great red banner with seven fringes;
translations.idiomatic: its boushan ornaments, wheel covers, and luo belts were all scarlet, and it bore the great red banner with seven fringes;

sentences.zh: 駕赤馬六，駕士一百五十四人。

translations.literal: Drawn by six red horses; carriage attendants one hundred fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Six red horses drew it, with one hundred fifty-four carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 革輅淺黃白色，飾以金塗銅，製如象輅；

translations.literal: The leather carriage pale yellow-white in color, decorated with gold-plated copper, its design like the ivory carriage;
translations.idiomatic: The leather carriage was pale yellow-white and ornamented with gold-plated copper in the same design as the ivory carriage;

sentences.zh: 博山、輪衣、絡帶並以淺黃白，建大白六斿；

translations.literal: Boushan ornaments, wheel covers, and luo belts all pale yellow-white; raises the great white banner with six fringes;
translations.idiomatic: its boushan ornaments, wheel covers, and luo belts were all pale yellow-white, and it bore the great white banner with six fringes;

sentences.zh: 駕黃白馬六，駕士百五十四人。

translations.literal: Drawn by six yellow-white horses; carriage attendants one hundred fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Six yellow-white horses drew it, with one hundred fifty-four carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 木輅黑色，飾以金塗銀，製如革輅；

translations.literal: The wood carriage black in color, decorated with gold-plated silver, its design like the leather carriage;
translations.idiomatic: The wood carriage was black and ornamented with gold-plated silver in the same design as the leather carriage;

sentences.zh: 博山、輪衣、絡帶並以黑，建大麾四斿；

translations.literal: Boushan ornaments, wheel covers, and luo belts all black; raises the great standard with four fringes;
translations.idiomatic: its boushan ornaments, wheel covers, and luo belts were all black, and it bore the great standard with four fringes;

sentences.zh: 駕黑馬六，駕士一百五十四人。

translations.literal: Drawn by six black horses; carriage attendants one hundred fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Six black horses drew it, with one hundred fifty-four carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 五輅駕士服色：平巾幘、青絹抹額、纈絹對花鳳袍、緋纈絹對花寬袖襖、羅襪絹袴、襪、麻鞋，其色各從其輅。

translations.literal: The dress colors of the five-carriage attendants: plain kerchief cap, azure silk forehead cloth, tie-dyed silk facing-flower phoenix robe, scarlet tie-dyed silk facing-flower wide-sleeved jacket, silk socks and silk trousers, leg wrappings, hemp shoes—their colors each following its carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The five-carriage attendants wore plain kerchief caps, azure silk forehead cloths, tie-dyed silk phoenix robes with facing flowers, scarlet tie-dyed wide-sleeved jackets with facing flowers, silk socks and trousers, leg wrappings, and hemp shoes, each color matching its carriage.

sentences.zh: 大輅。

translations.literal: The great imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，徐秉哲言：“南北郊，皇帝乘玉輅以赴齋宮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, Xu Bingzhe said: "For the southern and northern suburban sacrifices, the emperor rides the jade carriage to reach the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhenghe reign, Xu Bingzhe said, "At the southern and northern suburban sacrifices, the emperor rides the jade carriage to the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 自齋宮赴壇，正當祀天祭地，乃乘大輦，疑非禮意。”

translations.literal: From the fasting palace to the altar, precisely when sacrificing to Heaven and offering to Earth, he then rides the great palanquin—this seems not to accord with ritual intent."
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the fasting palace to the altar, at the very moment of sacrificing to Heaven and offering to Earth, he rides the great palanquin instead— which seems at odds with ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 下禮製局討論。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Bureau for Ritual Regulations for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Bureau for Ritual Regulations for discussion.

sentences.zh: 禮製局請：“造大輅如玉輅之製，唯不飾以玉。

translations.literal: The Bureau for Ritual Regulations requested: "Construct a great imperial carriage following the jade carriage's design, only without jade ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau for Ritual Regulations proposed, "Construct a great imperial carriage after the jade carriage's design, but without jade ornament.

sentences.zh: 所駕之馬，其數如之，唯樊纓一就，以稱尚質之義。

translations.literal: The horses that draw it, their number the same, but bridle tassels of only one set, to accord with the principle of esteeming substance.
translations.idiomatic: The number of horses should match, but with only one set of bridle tassels, in keeping with the principle of esteeming substance.

sentences.zh: 仍建大旂十有二旒，龍章日月，以協象天之義。

translations.literal: Still raise the great banner with twelve fringes, dragon emblems and sun and moon, to accord with the principle of symbolizing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It should still bear the great banner with twelve fringes, emblazoned with dragons, the sun, and the moon, to accord with the symbolism of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 至禮畢還齋宮，則禦大輦，於禮無嫌。”

translations.literal: When the rites are complete and he returns to the fasting palace, then ride the great palanquin—in ritual there is no objection."
translations.idiomatic: When the rites are finished and he returns to the fasting palace, he may ride the great palanquin without ritual objection.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 大輦。

translations.literal: The great palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 《周官》巾車氏有輦車，以人組挽之，宮中從容所乘。

translations.literal: The Director of Carriages in the Rites of Zhou had palanquin carriages, drawn by human teams—what one rode at leisure within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou's Director of Carriages had palanquin carriages drawn by human teams—the vehicle used at leisure within the palace.

sentences.zh: 唐製，輦有七：一曰大鳳輦，二曰大芳輦，三曰仙遊輦，四曰小輕輦，五曰芳亭輦，六曰大玉輦，七曰小玉輦。

translations.literal: Tang institutions: palanquins numbered seven—first the great phoenix palanquin, second the great fragrant palanquin, third the immortal-roaming palanquin, fourth the small light palanquin, fifth the fragrant pavilion palanquin, sixth the great jade palanquin, seventh the small jade palanquin.
