translations.idiomatic: Under Tang institutions there were seven palanquins: the great phoenix palanquin, the great fragrant palanquin, the immortal-roaming palanquin, the small light palanquin, the fragrant pavilion palanquin, the great jade palanquin, and the small jade palanquin.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆四年，翰林學士承旨陶穀為禮儀使，創意造為大輦：赤質，正方，油畫，金塗銀葉，龍鳳裝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong under Emperor Taizu, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts Tao Gu served as Commissioner of Ritual and devised the great palanquin: red substance, square, oil-painted, gold-plated silver leaf, dragon-and-phoenix ornament.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts Tao Gu, serving as Commissioner of Ritual, devised the great palanquin: red in substance, square, oil-painted, with gold-plated silver leaf and dragon-and-phoenix ornament.

sentences.zh: 其上四面行龍雲氣，火珠方鑒，銀絲囊網，珠翠結絛，雲龍鈿窠霞子。

translations.literal: Upon it on four sides running dragons and cloud vapor, fire pearls and square mirrors, silver-thread pouch nets, pearl-and-jade knotted cords, cloud-dragon inlaid-cell rosy clouds.
translations.idiomatic: On all four sides ran dragons amid cloud vapor, with fire pearls and square mirrors, silver-thread pouch nets, pearl-and-jade knotted cords, and cloud-dragon inlaid rosy cloud motifs.

sentences.zh: 四角龍頭銜香囊，頂輪施耀葉。

translations.literal: At the four corners dragon heads holding incense pouches; on the crown wheel radiant leaves were affixed.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon heads at the four corners held incense pouches, and radiant leaves adorned the crown wheel.

sentences.zh: 中有銀蓮花坐龍，紅綾裏，碧牙壓帖。

translations.literal: Within was a silver lotus-seat dragon, lined with red silk, with green ivory pressure plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Within stood a silver lotus-seat dragon, lined with red silk and fitted with green ivory pressure plaques.

sentences.zh: 內設圓鑒，銀絲香囊，銀飾勾闌、台坐，紅絲絛網，分錔。

translations.literal: Inside were set round mirrors, silver-thread incense pouches, silver-decorated railings and platform seats, red silk cord nets, and corner plates.
translations.idiomatic: Inside were round mirrors, silver-thread incense pouches, silver-decorated railings and platform seats, red silk cord nets, and corner plates.

sentences.zh: 中施黃褥，上置御坐，扶幾，香爐，錦結綬。

translations.literal: Within was spread a yellow cushion; above were placed the imperial seat, arm-support table, incense burner, and brocade knotted sashes.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow cushion was spread within, above which stood the imperial seat, an arm-support table, an incense burner, and brocade knotted sashes.

sentences.zh: 幾衣、輪衣、絡帶並緋繡壓金銀線。

translations.literal: Table covers, wheel covers, and luo belts all scarlet embroidered with pressed gold and silver thread.
translations.idiomatic: The table covers, wheel covers, and luo belts were all scarlet embroidered with gold and silver thread.

sentences.zh: 長竿四，銀裹鐵鋦龍頭，魚鉤，錦膊褥，銀裝畫梯，拓叉，黃羅緣席、褥、帕，梯杖褥，朱索，緋繒油帕。

translations.literal: Long poles four, silver-wrapped iron-clamped dragon heads, fish hooks, brocade shoulder cushions, silver-fitted painted ladders, spreading forks, yellow gauze-edged mats, cushions, and cloths, ladder-pole cushions, vermilion cords, scarlet silk oil cloths.
translations.idiomatic: Four long poles bore silver-wrapped, iron-clamped dragon heads, fish hooks, brocade shoulder cushions, silver-fitted painted ladders, and spreading forks, with yellow gauze-edged mats, cushions, and cloths, ladder-pole cushions, vermilion cords, and scarlet oiled silk cloths.

sentences.zh: 主輦六十四人。

translations.literal: Palanquin bearers sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-four men bore the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 親祀南郊、謁太廟還及具鸞駕黃麾仗、省方還都，則乘之。

translations.literal: When personally sacrificing at the southern suburb, returning from visiting the Imperial Ancestral Temple, or when fully arraying the luan escort with yellow-banner guard, or returning to the capital from inspecting the realm, then one rides it.
translations.idiomatic: It was ridden on returning from personally sacrificing at the southern suburb or visiting the Imperial Ancestral Temple, when the luan escort and yellow-banner guard were fully deployed, or on returning to the capital from touring the realm.

sentences.zh: 真宗東封，以舊輦太重，遂命別造，凡減七百餘斤，後常用焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong performed the eastern Feng sacrifice, because the old palanquin was too heavy, he ordered a separate one made, reducing the weight by more than seven hundred jin in all; afterward it was regularly used.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong performed the eastern Feng sacrifice, the old palanquin proved too heavy, so he ordered a new one built, shedding more than seven hundred jin; thereafter this became the regular vehicle.

sentences.zh: 神宗已後，其製：赤質，正方，油畫，金塗銀龍鳳裝，朱漆天輪一，金塗銀頂龍一。

translations.literal: After Emperor Shenzong, its design: red substance, square, oil-painted, gold-plated silver dragon-and-phoenix ornament, one vermilion-lacquered heaven wheel, one gold-plated silver crown dragon.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shenzong its design was: red in substance, square, oil-painted, with gold-plated silver dragon-and-phoenix ornament, one vermilion-lacquered heaven wheel, and one gold-plated silver crown dragon.

sentences.zh: 四面施行龍一十六，火珠四。

translations.literal: On four sides running dragons sixteen, fire pearls four.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen running dragons adorned the four sides, with four fire pearls.

sentences.zh: 四角龍頭四，穗球一十二。

translations.literal: Dragon heads at the four corners four; tassel balls twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Four dragon heads stood at the corners, with twelve tassel balls.

sentences.zh: 頂輪施耀葉，紅羅輪衣一，綴銀鈴，紅羅絡帶二。

translations.literal: On the crown wheel radiant leaves were affixed; one red gauze wheel cover, hung with silver bells; two red gauze luo belts.
translations.idiomatic: Radiant leaves adorned the crown wheel; there was one red gauze wheel cover hung with silver bells and two red gauze luo belts.

sentences.zh: 中設御坐、曲幾、錦褥等，施屏風，香爐，結綬。

translations.literal: Within were set the imperial seat, curved table, brocade cushion, and the like; a screen was installed, an incense burner, and knotted sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Within stood the imperial seat, curved table, brocade cushion, and the like, together with a screen, incense burner, and knotted sashes.

sentences.zh: 長竿四，飾以金塗銀龍頭。

translations.literal: Long poles four, ornamented with gold-plated silver dragon heads.
translations.idiomatic: Four long poles were ornamented with gold-plated silver dragon heads.

sentences.zh: 祀畢，車駕還內，若不進輅，則乘大輦。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice is complete and the imperial carriage returns within the palace, if one does not enter a ceremonial carriage, then one rides the great palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was finished and the imperial procession returned within the palace, if the emperor did not mount a ceremonial carriage, he rode the great palanquin.

sentences.zh: 政和之製：黃質，冒以黃衣，紘以黃帶。

translations.literal: The Zhenghe design: yellow substance, covered with yellow cloth, bound with yellow cords.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenghe design was yellow in substance, covered with yellow cloth and bound with yellow cords.

sentences.zh: 車箱四圍，於桯之外，高二尺二寸。

translations.literal: The carriage box on four sides, outside the side rails, two chi two cun in height.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage box rose two chi two cun on all four sides beyond the side rails.

sentences.zh: 設軾於前楹，軾高三尺二寸。

translations.literal: A shi rail was set at the front pillar; the shi three chi two cun in height.
translations.idiomatic: A shi rail was set at the front pillar, three chi two cun high.

sentences.zh: 建大旂於後楹，旂十二斿，其長曳地，其色黃，繪以交龍；

translations.literal: The great banner was raised at the rear pillar; the banner twelve fringes, its length trailing on the ground, its color yellow, painted with interlaced dragons;
translations.idiomatic: The great banner was raised at the rear pillar with twelve fringes trailing to the ground, yellow in color and painted with interlaced dragons;

sentences.zh: 素帛為縿，繪以日月，以弧張幅，以韣韜弧；

translations.literal: Plain silk formed the lower section, painted with sun and moon; a bow stretched the panel, and a bow case sheathed the bow;
translations.idiomatic: plain silk formed the lower section, painted with the sun and moon; a bow stretched the panel, and a bow case sheathed the bow;

sentences.zh: 杠以青錦綢之，注旄於竿首，係以鈴。

translations.literal: The pole was wrapped in azure brocade; an ox-tail pennant was affixed at the pole head, with bells attached.
translations.idiomatic: the pole was wrapped in azure brocade, an ox-tail pennant affixed at its head, and bells attached.

sentences.zh: 國朝之輦有七，中興後，唯存大輦、平輦、逍遙三輦而已。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's palanquins numbered seven; after the Restoration, only the great palanquin, level palanquin, and free-roaming palanquin remained.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty once had seven palanquins; after the Restoration only the great palanquin, level palanquin, and free-roaming palanquin survived.

sentences.zh: 大輦又曰大安輦，其製：赤質，正方，高十五尺三寸，方十一尺六寸。

translations.literal: The great palanquin was also called the Great Peace Palanquin; its design: red substance, square, fifteen chi three cun in height, eleven chi six cun square.
translations.idiomatic: The great palanquin, also called the Great Peace Palanquin, was red in substance and square, fifteen chi three cun high and eleven chi six cun across.

sentences.zh: 四柱，平盤，上覆青綠錦。

translations.literal: Four pillars, a level platform, covered above with azure-green brocade.
translations.idiomatic: It had four pillars and a level platform covered with azure-green brocade.

sentences.zh: 上有天輪三層，外施金塗銀博山八十一。

translations.literal: Above was a heaven wheel of three layers; on the outside were affixed eighty-one gold-plated silver boushan ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Above stood a three-layer heaven wheel with eighty-one gold-plated silver boushan ornaments on the outside.

sentences.zh: 內有圓鏡，金塗銀頂龍一，四面行龍十六，火珠四。

translations.literal: Within was a round mirror, one gold-plated silver crown dragon, running dragons on four sides sixteen, fire pearls four.
translations.idiomatic: Within was a round mirror, one gold-plated silver crown dragon, sixteen running dragons on the four sides, and four fire pearls.

sentences.zh: 輪衣以青，墜以金鈴，頂有青羅十字分垂四角，曰絡帶。

translations.literal: The wheel cover was azure; hung with gold bells; at the top azure gauze in a cross pattern hung down at the four corners—called luo belts.
translations.idiomatic: The wheel cover was azure and hung with gold bells; at the top azure gauze hung in a cross pattern from the four corners—these were called luo belts.

sentences.zh: 四角出龍首，銜氂牛五色尾，曰旒綏。

translations.literal: At the four corners dragon heads projected, holding yak tails of five colors—called liu-sui streamers.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon heads projected from the four corners, holding five-colored yak tails—these were called liu-sui streamers.

sentences.zh: 四面拱鬥，外施方鏡，九柱圍以朱闌，中設御坐、曲幾、屏風、錦褥。

translations.literal: On four sides bracket-arm canopy structure; square mirrors affixed outside; nine pillars enclosed by vermilion railings; within were set the imperial seat, curved table, screen, and brocade cushion.
translations.idiomatic: Bracket-arm canopy structure rose on all four sides with square mirrors affixed outside; nine pillars enclosed by vermilion railings held the imperial seat, curved table, screen, and brocade cushion within.

sentences.zh: 下舉以長竿四，攢竹筋膠丹漆之，竿為龍首。

translations.literal: Below it was borne on four long poles, bamboo ribs bundled and glued with cinnabar lacquer; the poles formed dragon heads.
translations.idiomatic: Below, four long poles bore it; bamboo ribs were bundled and lacquered cinnabar-red, the pole ends shaped as dragon heads.

sentences.zh: 平盤下，四圍結紅絲網。

translations.literal: Beneath the level platform, on four sides a red silk net was knotted.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the level platform a red silk net was knotted on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 輦官服色：武弁，黃纈對鳳袍，黃絹勒帛，紫生色袒帶，紫絹行縢。

translations.literal: Palanquin officers' dress colors: military cap, yellow tie-dyed facing-phoenix robe, yellow silk waist band, purple raw-silk sash, purple silk leg bindings.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin officers wore military caps, yellow tie-dyed phoenix robes with facing patterns, yellow silk waist bands, purple raw-silk sashes, and purple silk leg bindings.

sentences.zh: 芳亭輦，黑質，頂如幕屋，緋羅衣，裙襴、絡帶皆繡雲鳳。

translations.literal: The Fragrant Pavilion Palanquin: black substance, its top like a tent house, scarlet gauze covering; skirt panels and luo belts all embroidered with cloud phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: The Fragrant Pavilion Palanquin was black in substance with a tent-like top and scarlet gauze covering; its skirt panels and luo belts were all embroidered with cloud phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 兩面朱綠窗花版，外施紅絲網綢，金銅分錔，前後垂簾，下設牙床、勾闌。

translations.literal: On two sides vermilion-green window flower panels; outside a red silk net was draped, gold-and-copper corner plates; curtains hung front and rear; below were set ivory bed and railings.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion-green window panels adorned both sides; outside hung a red silk net with gold-and-copper corner plates; curtains draped front and rear; below stood an ivory bed and railings.

sentences.zh: 長竿四，銀龍頭，銀飾梯，行馬。

translations.literal: Long poles four, silver dragon heads, silver-decorated ladders, walking-horse supports.
translations.idiomatic: Four long poles bore silver dragon heads, silver-decorated ladders, and walking-horse supports.

sentences.zh: 主輦一百二十人。

translations.literal: Palanquin bearers one hundred twenty.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred twenty men bore the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 政和之製，簾以紅羅繡鵝為額，內設御坐，長竿飾以金塗銅螭首，橫竿三。

translations.literal: The Zhenghe design: the curtain had a red gauze embroidered goose as its heading; within the imperial seat was set; long poles ornamented with gold-plated copper ch'i heads; cross poles three.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe design the curtain heading was embroidered with a goose in red gauze; the imperial seat was set within; long poles bore gold-plated copper ch'i heads; there were three cross poles.

sentences.zh: 鳳輦，赤質，頂輪下有二柱，緋羅輪衣，絡帶、門簾皆繡雲鳳。

translations.literal: The Phoenix Palanquin: red substance; beneath the crown wheel two pillars; scarlet gauze wheel cover; luo belts and door curtains all embroidered with cloud phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: The Phoenix Palanquin was red in substance; beneath the crown wheel stood two pillars; its scarlet gauze wheel cover, luo belts, and door curtains were all embroidered with cloud phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 頂有金鳳一，兩壁刻畫龜文、金鳳翅。

translations.literal: On the top one gold phoenix; on two walls tortoise patterns and gold phoenix wings were carved and painted.
translations.idiomatic: One gold phoenix crowned the top; tortoise patterns and gold phoenix wings were carved and painted on both walls.

sentences.zh: 前有軾匱、香爐、香寶、結帶，下有勾闌二重，內設紅錦褥。

translations.literal: In front were shi compartment, incense burner, incense treasure, and knotted sashes; below double railings; within a red brocade cushion was set.
translations.idiomatic: In front stood a shi compartment, incense burner, incense treasure, and knotted sashes; below were double railings, with a red brocade cushion within.

sentences.zh: 長竿三，銀飾梯，行馬。

translations.literal: Long poles three, silver-decorated ladders, walking-horse supports.
translations.idiomatic: Three long poles bore silver-decorated ladders and walking-horse supports.

sentences.zh: 主輦八十人。

translations.literal: Palanquin bearers eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty men bore the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 法駕鹵簿，不設鳳輦。

translations.literal: In the statutory escort guard of honor, the phoenix palanquin was not deployed.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix palanquin was not included in the statutory escort guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 逍遙輦，以棕櫚為屋，赤質，金塗銀裝，朱漆扶版二，雲版一，長竿二，飾以金塗銀龍頭。

translations.literal: The Free-Roaming Palanquin: palm fronds formed the canopy; red substance; gold-plated silver fittings; two vermilion-lacquered handrails, one cloud panel; long poles two, ornamented with gold-plated silver dragon heads.
translations.idiomatic: The Free-Roaming Palanquin had a palm-frond canopy, red substance, and gold-plated silver fittings; two vermilion-lacquered handrails and one cloud panel; two long poles ornamented with gold-plated silver dragon heads.

sentences.zh: 常行幸所禦。

translations.literal: What one regularly rides on imperial progresses.
translations.idiomatic: It was the vehicle regularly used on imperial progresses.

sentences.zh: 又魚鉤，分錔，梅紅絛。

translations.literal: Also fish hooks, corner plates, and plum-red cords.
translations.idiomatic: It also had fish hooks, corner plates, and plum-red cords.

sentences.zh: 輦官十二人，春夏服緋羅衫，秋冬服白師子錦襖。

translations.literal: Palanquin officers twelve; in spring and summer they wore scarlet gauze shirts, in autumn and winter white lion-pattern brocade jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve palanquin officers wore scarlet gauze shirts in spring and summer and white lion-pattern brocade jackets in autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 東封，別造辟塵逍遙輦，加窗隔，黃繒為裏，賜名省方逍遙輦。

translations.literal: For the eastern Feng sacrifice a separate dust-repelling free-roaming palanquin was made, with window partitions added and yellow silk as lining; it was granted the name Provincial Tour Free-Roaming Palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: For the eastern Feng sacrifice a separate dust-repelling free-roaming palanquin was built with window partitions and a yellow silk lining; it was granted the name Provincial Tour Free-Roaming Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 中興之製，赤質，金塗四柱，棕屋上有走脊金龍四，中起火珠凸頂，四面不設窗障，中有禦踏子，製甚簡素。

translations.literal: The Restoration design: red substance; four gold-plated pillars; on the palm canopy four running-ridge gold dragons; in the center a fire-pearl convex crown; on four sides no window screens were set; within an imperial footrest; the design very simple and plain.
translations.idiomatic: The Restoration design was red in substance with four gold-plated pillars; four running-ridge gold dragons crowned the palm canopy, with a fire-pearl convex top at the center; no window screens were set on any side; an imperial footrest stood within—the design was notably plain.

sentences.zh: 祗應人員服帽子、宜男方勝纈衫。

translations.literal: Attendant personnel wore caps and Yi-ma-style square-pattern tie-dye shirts.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants wore caps and square-pattern tie-dye shirts in the Yi-ma style.

sentences.zh: 平輦，又名平頭輦，亦曰太平輦，飾如逍遙輦而無屋。

translations.literal: The Level Palanquin, also called the Flat-Top Palanquin and also the Great Peace Palanquin, ornamented like the free-roaming palanquin but without a canopy house.
translations.idiomatic: The Level Palanquin, also called the Flat-Top Palanquin or Great Peace Palanquin, was ornamented like the free-roaming palanquin but without a canopy house.

sentences.zh: 輦官十二人，服同逍遙輦。

translations.literal: Palanquin officers twelve; dress the same as the free-roaming palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve palanquin officers wore the same dress as those of the free-roaming palanquin.

sentences.zh: 常行幸所禦。

translations.literal: What one regularly rides on imperial progresses.
translations.idiomatic: It was the vehicle regularly used on imperial progresses.

sentences.zh: 東封，別造升山天平輦，施機關，賜名曰登封輦。

translations.literal: For the eastern Feng sacrifice a separate mountain-ascending level palanquin was made, fitted with mechanisms; it was granted the name Ascent-to-the-Feng Palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: For the eastern Feng sacrifice a separate mountain-ascending level palanquin was built with mechanical fittings; it was granted the name Ascent-to-the-Feng Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 中興之製，赤質，正方，形如一朱龍椅而加長竿二，飾如逍遙輦而不施棕屋，製尤簡素，止施畫雲版而已。

translations.literal: The Restoration design: red substance, square, shaped like a vermilion dragon chair with two long poles added; ornamented like the free-roaming palanquin but without a palm canopy; the design especially simple and plain, bearing only painted cloud panels.
translations.idiomatic: The Restoration design was red, square, and shaped like a vermilion dragon chair with two long poles added; it was ornamented like the free-roaming palanquin but without a palm canopy—the design was especially plain, bearing only painted cloud panels.

sentences.zh: 又有七寶輦，隆興二年，為德壽宮所製也。

translations.literal: There was also the Seven Treasures Palanquin, made in the second year of Longxing for the Virtuous Longevity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Seven Treasures Palanquin, made in the second year of Longxing for the Virtuous Longevity Palace.

sentences.zh: 高五十一寸，闊二十七寸，深三十六寸。

translations.literal: Height fifty-one cun, width twenty-seven cun, depth thirty-six cun.
translations.idiomatic: It was fifty-one cun high, twenty-seven cun wide, and thirty-six cun deep.

sentences.zh: 比附大輦、平輦制度為之。

translations.literal: It was made by analogy to the regulations of the great palanquin and level palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: It was made according to the regulations of the great and level palanquins.

sentences.zh: 上施頂輪、耀葉、角龍、頂龍、滴子、鐸子、結穗球。

translations.literal: Above were affixed crown wheel, radiant leaves, corner dragons, crown dragon, pendant drops, bell pendants, and knotted tassel balls.
translations.idiomatic: Above it bore a crown wheel, radiant leaves, corner dragons, crown dragon, pendant drops, bell pendants, and knotted tassel balls.

sentences.zh: 下施梅紅絲裙網，加綴七寶，中設香木御坐，引手為轉身龍，靠背為龍首，靠枰子織以紅黃藤。

translations.literal: Below was a plum-red silk skirt net, with seven treasures added in interspersed ornament; within a fragrant-wood imperial seat was set; the armrest formed a turning-body dragon; the backrest formed a dragon head; the back panel was woven with red and yellow rattan.
translations.idiomatic: Below hung a plum-red silk skirt net interspersed with seven treasures; within stood a fragrant-wood imperial seat whose armrest formed a coiling dragon and whose backrest formed a dragon head; the back panel was woven with red and yellow rattan.

sentences.zh: 舁以長竿二，竿為螭首，金塗銀飾焉。

translations.literal: It was borne on two long poles; the poles formed ch'i heads, with gold-plated silver ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Two long poles bore it, their ends shaped as ch'i heads with gold-plated silver ornament.

sentences.zh: 初，有司言：“東都舊制，輦飾以玉，裙網用七寶，而滴子用真珠。”

translations.literal: At first the responsible officials said: "Under the old Eastern Capital regulations, the palanquin was ornamented with jade, the skirt net used seven treasures, and the pendant drops used genuine pearls."
translations.idiomatic: At first the responsible officials said, "Under the old Eastern Capital regulations, the palanquin was ornamented with jade, the skirt net used seven treasures, and the pendant drops were of genuine pearls."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“上皇意不然，止欲簡素。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The retired emperor's intent was otherwise; he wished only for simplicity."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The retired emperor did not agree; he wanted only simplicity."

sentences.zh: 遂以塗金易玉，梅紅絲結裙網，間綴七寶，而象牙易真珠。

translations.literal: Thereupon gilding replaced jade, plum-red silk formed the knotted skirt net with seven treasures interspersed, and ivory replaced genuine pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon gilded ornament replaced jade, a plum-red silk knotted skirt net was interspersed with seven treasures, and ivory replaced genuine pearls.

sentences.zh: 既而上皇卻不受，每至大內，多乘馬，而間有行幸，則用肩輿。

translations.literal: Yet afterward the retired emperor still would not accept it; whenever he came to the inner palace he mostly rode a horse, and on occasional imperial progresses he used a shoulder sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the retired emperor still would not accept it; whenever he entered the inner palace he mostly rode horseback, and on occasional progresses he used a shoulder sedan instead.

sentences.zh: 自是，重華、壽康兩宮並不別造。

translations.literal: From this time, neither the Chonghua nor the Shoukang palace had separate ones made.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter neither the Chonghua nor the Shoukang palace had separate palanquins made.

sentences.zh: 小輿，赤質，頂輪下施曲柄如蓋，緋繡輪衣、絡帶，製如鳳輦而小。

translations.literal: The small sedan: red substance; beneath the crown wheel a curved handle like a canopy was affixed; scarlet embroidered wheel cover and luo belts; its design like the phoenix palanquin but smaller.
translations.idiomatic: The small sedan was red in substance; beneath the crown wheel stood a curved handle like a canopy, with scarlet embroidered wheel cover and luo belts; its design matched the phoenix palanquin but on a smaller scale.

sentences.zh: 下有勾闌，牙床，繡瀝水。

translations.literal: Below were railings, an ivory bed, and embroidered pendant streamers.
translations.idiomatic: Below stood railings, an ivory bed, and embroidered pendant streamers.

sentences.zh: 中設方床，緋繡羅衣，錦褥。

translations.literal: Within a square bed was set, scarlet embroidered gauze covering, and brocade cushion.
translations.idiomatic: Within stood a square bed with scarlet embroidered gauze covering and a brocade cushion.

sentences.zh: 上有小案、坐床，皆繡衣。

translations.literal: Above were a small table and seat bed, all with embroidered covering.
translations.idiomatic: Above stood a small table and seat bed, all with embroidered covering.

sentences.zh: 踏床緋衣。

translations.literal: The footrest bed scarlet covering.
translations.idiomatic: The footrest bed had scarlet covering.

sentences.zh: 前後長竿二，銀飾梯，行馬。

translations.literal: Front and rear long poles two, silver-decorated ladders, walking-horse supports.
translations.idiomatic: Front and rear, two long poles bore silver-decorated ladders and walking-horse supports.

sentences.zh: 奉輿二十四人。

translations.literal: Sedan bearers twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four men bore the sedan.

sentences.zh: 中興後，去其輪蓋，方四十九寸，高三十一寸。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, its wheel canopy was removed; forty-nine cun square, thirty-one cun in height.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration its wheel canopy was removed; it was forty-nine cun square and thirty-one cun high.

sentences.zh: 輿上周以勾闌，施翟羽，玉照子，中為方床三級。

translations.literal: On the sedan's upper perimeter were railings; zhai feathers, yuzhao ornaments, and a three-tiered square bed were affixed at the center.
translations.idiomatic: Around the upper perimeter of the sedan stood railings; pheasant feathers and jade mirror ornaments were affixed, and at the center stood a three-tiered square bed.

sentences.zh: 上設御坐、曲幾、踏子，曲柄緋羅繡蓋，輿下紅絲結五色花裙網。

translations.literal: Above were set an imperial seat, curved armrest table, and footrest; a curved-handle scarlet gauze embroidered canopy; beneath the sedan a red-silk knotted five-colored floral skirt net.
translations.idiomatic: Above stood an imperial seat, a curved armrest table, and a footrest, beneath a curved-handle canopy of scarlet embroidered gauze; below the sedan hung a skirt net of red silk knotted in five-colored floral patterns.

sentences.zh: 舁以長竿二，竿為螭首。

translations.literal: It was borne on two long poles; the poles formed ch'i heads.
translations.idiomatic: Two long poles bore it, their ends shaped as ch'i heads.

sentences.zh: 宮殿從容所乘，設鹵簿則陳之。

translations.literal: Within the palace precincts it was the vehicle used at leisure; when the halu was deployed it was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace precincts it served for leisurely travel; when the ceremonial guard was deployed, it was displayed in procession.

sentences.zh: 腰輿，前後長竿各二，金銅螭頭，緋繡鳳裙襴，上施錦褥，別設小床，緋繡花龍衣。

translations.literal: The waist sedan: front and rear long poles two each, gold and bronze ch'i heads, scarlet embroidered phoenix skirt panels, above a brocade cushion was affixed, and a separate small bed was set with scarlet embroidered floral dragon covering.
translations.idiomatic: The waist sedan had two long poles fore and aft, their ends cast as gold and bronze ch'i heads; scarlet embroidered phoenix skirt panels hung below, a brocade cushion lay above, and a separate small bed was fitted with scarlet embroidered dragon-flower covering.

sentences.zh: 奉輿十六人。

translations.literal: Sedan bearers sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen men bore the sedan.

sentences.zh: 中興製，赤質，方形，四面曲闌，下結繡裙網。

translations.literal: Restoration-period design: red substance, square form, curved railings on four sides, below a knotted embroidered skirt net.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Restoration design it was red in substance and square in form, with curved railings on all four sides and a knotted embroidered skirt net below.

sentences.zh: 製如小輿，惟無翟尾、玉照子、三級床、曲柄蓋，而上設方禦床、曲幾，舁竿無螭首，用亦同小輿。

translations.literal: Its design was like the small sedan, only without zhai tail, yuzhao ornament, three-tier bed, or curved-handle canopy; above were set a square imperial bed and curved armrest table; the bearing poles had no ch'i heads; its use was also the same as the small sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Its design matched the small sedan, save that it lacked pheasant-tail ornament, jade mirror, three-tier bed, and curved-handle canopy; above stood a square imperial bed and curved armrest table, the bearing poles bore no ch'i heads, and its use was the same as the small sedan.

sentences.zh: 耕根車製，青質，蓋三層，餘如五輅之副。

translations.literal: Root-Ploughing Carriage design: green substance, three-layer canopy; the rest like the secondary carriages of the Five Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Root-Ploughing Carriage was green in substance with a three-tier canopy; otherwise it followed the design of the secondary Five Lu carriages.

sentences.zh: 駕六青馬，駕士四十人。

translations.literal: Drawn by six green horses; carriage attendants forty.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by six green horses and attended by forty drivers.

sentences.zh: 親祠具大駕、法駕鹵簿，並列於仗內；

translations.literal: For personal sacrifice it was furnished with the grand and formal procession halu, both arrayed within the guard.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices performed by the emperor in person, it was accompanied by the grand and formal procession guards, both arrayed within the ceremonial train;

sentences.zh: 若耕籍則乘之。

translations.literal: If ploughing the sacred field, then one rode it.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor ploughed the sacred field, he rode in it.

sentences.zh: 國朝之車，自耕根而下，凡十有五。

translations.literal: Carriages of the dynasty, from the Root-Ploughing Carriage downward, numbered fifteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's ceremonial carriages, from the Root-Ploughing Carriage downward, numbered fifteen in all.

sentences.zh: 南渡所存，惟耕根車一而已，其制度並同，惟駕士七十五人。

translations.literal: Of what survived after the crossing south, only one Root-Ploughing Carriage remained; its regulations were all the same, only the carriage attendants were seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: After the crossing south only one Root-Ploughing Carriage remained; its design was unchanged, though its attendants numbered seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 進賢車，古安車也。

translations.literal: The Advance-the-Worthy Carriage was the ancient comfort carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Advance-the-Worthy Carriage was the ancient comfort carriage.

sentences.zh: 太祖乾德元年改赤質，兩壁紗窗，擎耳，虛匱，一轅，緋幰衣，絡帶、門簾皆繡鳳，紅絲網。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande of Emperor Taizu it was changed to red substance; both walls had gauze windows, raised ears, hollow box, one yoke; scarlet canopy covering; luo belts and door curtains all embroidered with phoenixes; red silk net.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qiande era, Emperor Taizu changed it to red in substance, with gauze windows in both walls, raised ears, a hollow box, and a single yoke; its canopy covering, luo belts, and door curtains were all embroidered with phoenixes, and a red silk net hung below.

sentences.zh: 中設朱漆床，香案，紫綾案衣，緋繒裹免索，朱漆行馬。

translations.literal: Within were set a vermilion-lacquered bed, incense table, purple damask table covering, scarlet silk-wrapped restraint ropes, and vermilion-lacquered walking-horse supports.
translations.idiomatic: Within stood a vermilion-lacquered bed and incense table with purple damask table covering, scarlet silk-wrapped restraint ropes, and vermilion-lacquered walking-horse supports.

sentences.zh: 〈（凡車皆有免索、行馬。）〉

translations.literal: (All carriages had restraint ropes and walking-horse supports.)
translations.idiomatic: (All carriages had restraint ropes and walking-horse supports.)

sentences.zh: 駕四馬，駕士二十四人。

translations.literal: Drawn by four horses; carriage attendants twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by four horses and attended by twenty-four drivers.

sentences.zh: 明遠車，古四望車也，駕以牛。

translations.literal: The Clear-Distance Carriage was the ancient four-view carriage; it was drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: The Clear-Distance Carriage was the ancient four-view carriage, drawn by oxen.

sentences.zh: 太祖乾德元年改，仍舊四馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande of Emperor Taizu it was changed, yet still drawn by four horses as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qiande era Emperor Taizu revised it, though it was still drawn by four horses as before.

sentences.zh: 赤質，製如屋，重簷勾闌，上有金龍，四角垂銅鐸，上層四面垂簾，下層周以花版，三轅。

translations.literal: Red substance; its design like a house, with double eaves and railings; above was a golden dragon; at the four corners hung bronze bells; the upper tier had curtains hanging on four sides; the lower tier was encircled with floral panels; three yokes.
translations.idiomatic: It was red in substance and built like a house, with double eaves and railings; a golden dragon stood above, bronze bells hung from the four corners, curtains draped on all four sides of the upper tier, floral panels encircled the lower tier, and it had three yokes.

sentences.zh: 駕士四十人，服繡對鳳。

translations.literal: Carriage attendants forty; their garments embroidered with paired phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Forty attendants drove it, wearing garments embroidered with paired phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 羊車，古輦車也，亦為畫輪車，駕以牛。

translations.literal: The Ram Carriage was the ancient palanquin carriage; it was also a painted-wheel carriage, drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: The Ram Carriage was the ancient palanquin carriage, also called a painted-wheel carriage, and was drawn by oxen.

sentences.zh: 隋駕以果下馬，今亦駕以二小馬。

translations.literal: Under the Sui it was drawn by short-legged horses; now it is also drawn by two small horses.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui it had been drawn by short-legged horses; now it was drawn by two small horses.

sentences.zh: 赤質，兩壁畫龜文、金鳳翅，緋幰衣、絡帶、門簾皆繡瑞羊。

translations.literal: Red substance; both walls painted with tortoise patterns and golden phoenix wings; scarlet canopy covering, luo belts, and door curtains all embroidered with auspicious rams.
translations.idiomatic: It was red in substance; both walls were painted with tortoise patterns and golden phoenix wings; its canopy covering, luo belts, and door curtains were all embroidered with auspicious rams.

sentences.zh: 童子十八人。

translations.literal: Pages eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen pages attended it.

sentences.zh: 指南車，一曰司南車。

translations.literal: The south-pointing carriage, also called the compass carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The south-pointing carriage, also called the compass carriage.

sentences.zh: 赤質，兩箱畫青龍、白虎，四面畫花鳥，重台，勾闌，鏤拱，四角垂香囊。

translations.literal: Red substance; both boxes painted with blue dragon and white tiger; on four sides painted flowers and birds; double platform, railings, carved bracket arms; at the four corners hung incense pouches.
translations.idiomatic: It was red in substance; both boxes were painted with the blue dragon and white tiger, flowers and birds adorned all four sides, and it had a double platform, railings, carved bracket arms, and incense pouches hanging from the four corners.

sentences.zh: 上有仙人，車雖轉而手常南指。

translations.literal: Above was an immortal; though the carriage turned, his hand always pointed south.
translations.idiomatic: Above stood an immortal figure whose arm always pointed south, no matter how the carriage turned.

sentences.zh: 一轅。

translations.literal: One yoke.
translations.idiomatic: It had a single yoke.

sentences.zh: 鳳首，駕四馬。

translations.literal: Phoenix head; drawn by four horses.
translations.idiomatic: Its yoke end was shaped as a phoenix head, and it was drawn by four horses.

sentences.zh: 駕士舊十八人，太宗雍熙四年，增為三十人。

translations.literal: Carriage attendants formerly eighteen; in the fourth year of Yongxi of Emperor Taizong, increased to thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Its attendants had formerly numbered eighteen; in the fourth year of the Yongxi era, Emperor Taizong increased them to thirty.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖五年，工部郎中燕肅始造指南車，肅上奏曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiansheng of Emperor Renzong, Yan Su, Director in the Ministry of Works, first constructed a south-pointing carriage; Su memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Tiansheng era, Yan Su, Director in the Ministry of Works, built the first south-pointing carriage and memorialized the throne, saying:

sentences.zh: 黃帝與蚩尤戰於涿鹿之野，蚩尤起大霧，軍士不知所向，帝遂作指南車。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu; Chiyou raised a great fog, and the soldiers did not know which way to go; the Emperor therefore made a south-pointing carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Emperor fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu, Chiyou raised a great fog so that the soldiers lost their way; the Emperor therefore devised the south-pointing carriage.

sentences.zh: 周成王時，越裳氏重譯來獻，使者惑失道，周公賜軿車以指南。

translations.literal: In the time of King Cheng of Zhou, the Yuechang clan came bearing tribute through repeated translation; the envoys lost their way in confusion; the Duke of Zhou granted them a light carriage to point the way south.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of King Cheng of Zhou, envoys of the Yuechang clan arrived with tribute through successive interpreters; when they lost their way, the Duke of Zhou granted them a light carriage to guide them south.

sentences.zh: 其後，法俱亡。

translations.literal: Afterward, the methods were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the methods were all lost.

sentences.zh: 漢張衡、魏馬鈞繼作之，屬世亂離，其器不存。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng of Han and Ma Jun of Wei successively made them again; as the age fell into turmoil and separation, the devices did not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng of Han and Ma Jun of Wei later reconstructed them, but amid the turmoil of the age the devices did not survive.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝平長安，嚐為此車，而製不精。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song pacified Chang'an, he once had such a carriage made, but its construction was not refined.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song pacified Chang'an, he once had such a carriage made, but its workmanship was crude.

sentences.zh: 祖衝之亦復造之。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi also made it again.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also reconstructed one.

sentences.zh: 後魏太武帝使郭善明造，彌年不就，命扶風馬嶽造，垂成而為善明鴆死，其法遂絕。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu of Later Wei had Guo Shanming make one; a full year passed without completion; he ordered Fufeng Ma Yue to make it; when it was nearly finished, Shanming was poisoned to death, and the method was thereby lost.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei ordered Guo Shanming to build one, but a full year passed without success; he then ordered Ma Yue of Fufeng to take over, and when the work was nearly complete Guo Shanming was poisoned to death, so the method was lost.

sentences.zh: 唐元和中，典作官金公立以其車及記裏鼓上之，憲宗閱於麟德殿，以備法駕，曆五代至國朝，不聞得其製者，今創意成之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Tang, the director of works Jin Gongli presented his carriage and li-drum carriage; Emperor Xianzong inspected them at Linde Hall to equip the formal procession; through the Five Dynasties to our dynasty, none were heard to have obtained the method; now by original design it has been completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era of Tang, Works Director Jin Gongli presented his south-pointing carriage and li-drum carriage; Emperor Xianzong inspected them at Linde Hall to equip the formal procession. From the Five Dynasties down to our dynasty, no one was known to have recovered the method; now I have completed it by original design.

sentences.zh: 其法：用獨轅車，車箱外籠上有重構，立木仙人於上，引臂南指。

translations.literal: Its method: use a single-yoke carriage; above the outer cage on the carriage box is a double structure; a wooden immortal is set upon it, extending an arm to point south.
translations.idiomatic: The method is this: a single-yoke carriage is used; atop the outer cage over the box stands a double structure bearing a wooden immortal with an outstretched arm pointing south.

sentences.zh: 用大小輪九，合齒一百二十。

translations.literal: Use large and small wheels nine; in total one hundred twenty teeth.
translations.idiomatic: It employs nine large and small wheels with one hundred twenty teeth in all.

sentences.zh: 足輪二，高六尺，圍一丈八尺。

translations.literal: Ground wheels two; height six chi, circumference one zhang eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: There are two ground wheels, six chi high with a circumference of one zhang eight chi.

sentences.zh: 附足立子輪二，徑二尺四寸，圍七尺二寸，出齒各二十四，齒間相去三寸。

translations.literal: Attached to the ground wheels, two upright subsidiary wheels; diameter two chi four cun, circumference seven chi two cun; projecting teeth twenty-four each; between teeth three cun apart.
translations.idiomatic: Attached to the ground wheels are two upright subsidiary wheels, two chi four cun in diameter and seven chi two cun in circumference, each with twenty-four projecting teeth spaced three cun apart.

sentences.zh: 轅端橫木下立小輪二，其徑三寸，鐵軸貫之。

translations.literal: Beneath the crossbar at the yoke end stand two small wheels; their diameter three cun; an iron axle passes through them.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the crossbar at the yoke end stand two small wheels three cun in diameter, pierced by an iron axle.

sentences.zh: 左小平輪一，其徑一尺二寸，出齒十二；

translations.literal: One left small flat wheel; its diameter one chi two cun; projecting teeth twelve;
translations.idiomatic: On the left is one small flat wheel, one chi two cun in diameter with twelve projecting teeth;

sentences.zh: 右小平輪一，其徑一尺二寸，出齒十二。

translations.literal: One right small flat wheel; its diameter one chi two cun; projecting teeth twelve.
translations.idiomatic: on the right is one small flat wheel, one chi two cun in diameter with twelve projecting teeth.

sentences.zh: 中心大平輪一，其徑四尺八寸，圍一丈四尺四寸，出齒四十八，齒間相去三寸。

translations.literal: One central large flat wheel; its diameter four chi eight cun, circumference one zhang four chi four cun; projecting teeth forty-eight; between teeth three cun apart.
translations.idiomatic: At the center is one large flat wheel, four chi eight cun in diameter with a circumference of one zhang four chi four cun, bearing forty-eight teeth spaced three cun apart.

sentences.zh: 中立貫心軸一，高八尺，徑三寸。

translations.literal: At the center stands one through-heart axle; height eight chi, diameter three cun.
translations.idiomatic: At the center stands a through-heart axle eight chi high and three cun in diameter.

sentences.zh: 上刻木為仙人，其車行，木人指南。

translations.literal: Above is carved wood forming an immortal; when the carriage moves, the wooden figure points south.
translations.idiomatic: A wooden immortal is carved above; as the carriage moves, the wooden figure points south.

sentences.zh: 若折而東，推轅右旋，附右足子輪順轉十二齒，擊右小平輪一匝，觸中心大平輪左旋四分之一，轉十二齒，車東行，木人交而南指。

translations.literal: If turning east, push the yoke to rotate right; the attached right ground subsidiary wheel turns forward twelve teeth, strikes the right small flat wheel one revolution, touches the central large flat wheel to rotate left one quarter, turning twelve teeth; the carriage goes east, and the wooden figure crosses over yet points south.
translations.idiomatic: If the carriage turns east, the yoke is pushed to the right; the right ground subsidiary wheel turns forward twelve teeth, driving the right small flat wheel one revolution, which turns the central large flat wheel one quarter leftward—twelve teeth—so that as the carriage moves east the wooden figure shifts position yet still points south.

sentences.zh: 若折而西，推轅左旋，附左足子輪隨輪順轉十二齒，擊左小平輪一匝，觸中心大平輪右轉四分之一，轉十二齒，車正西行，木人交而南指。

translations.literal: If turning west, push the yoke to rotate left; the attached left ground subsidiary wheel follows the wheel forward twelve teeth, strikes the left small flat wheel one revolution, touches the central large flat wheel to rotate right one quarter, turning twelve teeth; the carriage goes due west, and the wooden figure crosses over yet points south.
translations.idiomatic: If it turns west, the yoke is pushed to the left; the left ground subsidiary wheel turns forward twelve teeth, driving the left small flat wheel one revolution, which turns the central large flat wheel one quarter rightward—twelve teeth—so that as the carriage moves due west the wooden figure shifts position yet still points south.

sentences.zh: 若欲北行，或東，或西，轉亦如之。

translations.literal: If wishing to go north, or east, or west, the turning is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Whether turning north, east, or west, the mechanism works by the same principle.

sentences.zh: 詔以其法下有司製之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that this method be transmitted to the responsible offices for manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the responsible offices to manufacture it according to this method.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，內侍省吳德仁又獻指南車、記裏鼓車之製，二車成，其年宗祀大禮始用之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, Wu Deren of the Palace Attendant Office again presented the designs for the south-pointing carriage and li-drum carriage; when the two carriages were completed, that year they were first used in the great ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Daguan era, Wu Deren of the Palace Attendant Office submitted new designs for the south-pointing carriage and li-drum carriage; once both were completed, they were first used that year in the great ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其指南車身一丈一尺一寸五分，闊九尺五寸，深一丈九寸，車輪直徑五尺七寸，車轅一丈五寸。

translations.literal: Its south-pointing carriage body one zhang one chi one cun five fen, width nine chi five cun, depth one zhang nine cun; carriage wheel diameter five chi seven cun; carriage yoke one zhang five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The south-pointing carriage measured one zhang one chi one cun five fen in length, nine chi five cun in width, and one zhang nine cun in depth; its wheels were five chi seven cun in diameter and its yoke one zhang five cun long.

sentences.zh: 車箱上下為兩層，中設屏風，上安仙人一執仗，左右龜鶴各一，童子四各執纓立四角，上設關戾。

translations.literal: The carriage box was divided into upper and lower tiers; within a screen was set; above one immortal holding a staff was affixed; left and right one tortoise and one crane each; four pages each holding tassels stood at the four corners; above a latch mechanism was set.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage box had upper and lower tiers with a screen between; above stood one immortal bearing a staff, a tortoise and crane on left and right, four pages holding tassels at the four corners, and a latch mechanism mounted above.

sentences.zh: 臥輪一十三，各徑一尺八寸五分，圍五尺五寸五分，出齒三十二，齒間相去一寸八分。

translations.literal: Horizontal wheels thirteen; each diameter one chi eight cun five fen, circumference five chi five cun five fen; projecting teeth thirty-two; between teeth one cun eight fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: There were thirteen horizontal wheels, each one chi eight cun five fen in diameter with a circumference of five chi five cun five fen, bearing thirty-two teeth spaced one cun eight fen apart.

sentences.zh: 中心輪軸隨屏風貫下，下有輪一十三，中至大平輪。

translations.literal: The central wheel axle passed down through the screen; below were thirteen wheels, reaching at the center to the large flat wheel.
translations.idiomatic: The central wheel axle passed down through the screen; below were thirteen wheels leading at the center to the large flat wheel.

sentences.zh: 其輪徑三尺八寸，圍一丈一尺四寸，出齒一百，齒間相去一寸二分五厘，通上左右起落。

translations.literal: That wheel diameter three chi eight cun, circumference one zhang one chi four cun; projecting teeth one hundred; between teeth one cun two fen five li apart; passing above to left and right for rising and falling.
translations.idiomatic: That wheel was three chi eight cun in diameter with a circumference of one zhang one chi four cun, bearing one hundred teeth spaced one cun two fen five li apart, connecting above to left and right for engagement and disengagement.

sentences.zh: 二小平輪，各有鐵墜子一，皆徑一尺一寸，圍三尺三寸，出齒一十七，齒間相去一寸九分。

translations.literal: Two small flat wheels; each had one iron weight; all diameter one chi one cun, circumference three chi three cun; projecting teeth seventeen; between teeth one cun nine fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: Two small flat wheels, each with an iron weight, were one chi one cun in diameter with a circumference of three chi three cun, bearing seventeen teeth spaced one cun nine fen apart.

sentences.zh: 又左右附輪各一，徑一尺五寸五分，圍四尺六寸五分，出齒二十四，齒間相去二寸一分。

translations.literal: Further, one attached wheel on left and right each; diameter one chi five cun five fen, circumference four chi six cun five fen; projecting teeth twenty-four; between teeth two cun one fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: On left and right was one attached wheel each, one chi five cun five fen in diameter with a circumference of four chi six cun five fen, bearing twenty-four teeth spaced two cun one fen apart.

sentences.zh: 左右疊輪各二，下輪各徑二尺一寸，圍六尺三寸，出齒三十二，齒間相去二寸一分；

translations.literal: Left and right stacked wheels two each; lower wheels each diameter two chi one cun, circumference six chi three cun; projecting teeth thirty-two; between teeth two cun one fen apart;
translations.idiomatic: On left and right were two stacked wheels each; the lower wheels were two chi one cun in diameter with a circumference of six chi three cun, bearing thirty-two teeth spaced two cun one fen apart;

sentences.zh: 上輪各徑一尺二寸，圍三尺六寸，出齒三十二，齒間相去一寸一分。

translations.literal: Upper wheels each diameter one chi two cun, circumference three chi six cun; projecting teeth thirty-two; between teeth one cun one fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: the upper wheels were one chi two cun in diameter with a circumference of three chi six cun, bearing thirty-two teeth spaced one cun one fen apart.

sentences.zh: 左右車腳上各立輪一，徑二尺二寸，圍六尺六寸，出齒三十二，齒間相去二寸二分五厘。

translations.literal: On left and right beneath the carriage legs one wheel each was set upright; diameter two chi two cun, circumference six chi six cun; projecting teeth thirty-two; between teeth two cun two fen five li apart.
translations.idiomatic: On left and right, one wheel stood upright on each carriage leg, two chi two cun in diameter with a circumference of six chi six cun, bearing thirty-two teeth spaced two cun two fen five li apart.

sentences.zh: 左右後轅各小輪一，無齒，係竹{}並索在左右軸上，遇右轉使右轅小輪觸落右輪，若左轉使左轅小輪觸落左輪。

translations.literal: On left and right rear yokes one small wheel each, without teeth; tied with bamboo splints and ropes together on the left and right axles; when turning right, the right rear yoke's small wheel is made to touch and drop the right wheel; if turning left, the left rear yoke's small wheel is made to touch and drop the left wheel.
translations.idiomatic: On the left and right rear yokes stood one small toothless wheel each, lashed with bamboo splints and ropes to the left and right axles; when turning right, the right rear yoke's small wheel engaged and dropped the right wheel, and when turning left, the left rear yoke's small wheel engaged and dropped the left wheel.

sentences.zh: 行則仙童交而指南。

translations.literal: When moving, the immortal boy crosses over yet points south.
translations.idiomatic: In motion the immortal boy shifted position yet still pointed south.

sentences.zh: 車駕赤馬二，銅麵，插羽，鞶纓，攀胸鈴拂，緋絹屜，錦包尾。

translations.literal: The carriage was drawn by two red horses; copper face masks, inserted feathers, pankou tassels, chest bells and fans, scarlet silk saddle cloths, brocade-wrapped tails.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by two red horses with copper face masks, inserted feathers, pankou tassels, chest bells and fans, scarlet silk saddle cloths, and brocade-wrapped tails.

sentences.zh: 記裏鼓車，一名大章車。

translations.literal: The li-drum carriage, also called the Great Record Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The li-drum carriage, also called the Great Record Carriage.

sentences.zh: 赤質，四面畫花鳥，重台，勾闌，鏤拱。

translations.literal: Red substance; on four sides painted flowers and birds; double platform, railings, carved bracket arms.
translations.idiomatic: It was red in substance, painted with flowers and birds on all four sides, and had a double platform, railings, and carved bracket arms.

sentences.zh: 行一里，則上層木人擊鼓；

translations.literal: After traveling one li, then the upper-tier wooden figure strikes the drum;
translations.idiomatic: After traveling one li, the wooden figure on the upper tier struck the drum;

sentences.zh: 十里，則次層木人擊鐲。

translations.literal: Ten li, then the next-tier wooden figure strikes the gong.
translations.idiomatic: after ten li, the wooden figure on the next tier struck the gong.

sentences.zh: 一轅，鳳首，駕四馬。

translations.literal: One yoke, phoenix head; drawn by four horses.
translations.idiomatic: It had a single yoke ending in a phoenix head and was drawn by four horses.

sentences.zh: 駕士舊十八人，太宗雍熙四年，增為三十人。

translations.literal: Carriage attendants formerly eighteen; in the fourth year of Yongxi of Emperor Taizong, increased to thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Its attendants had formerly numbered eighteen; in the fourth year of the Yongxi era, Emperor Taizong increased them to thirty.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖五年，內侍盧道隆上記裏鼓車之製：“獨轅雙輪，箱上為兩重，各刻木為人，執木槌。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiansheng of Emperor Renzong, Palace Attendant Lu Daolong presented the design for the li-drum carriage: "Single yoke, double wheels; atop the box are two tiers, each carved with wooden figures holding wooden mallets.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Tiansheng era, Palace Attendant Lu Daolong submitted the design for the li-drum carriage: "It has a single yoke and two wheels; atop the box stand two tiers, each with carved wooden figures holding wooden mallets.

sentences.zh: 足輪各徑六尺，圍一丈八尺。

translations.literal: Ground wheels each diameter six chi, circumference one zhang eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: Each ground wheel is six chi in diameter with a circumference of one zhang eight chi.

sentences.zh: 足輪一周，而行地三步。

translations.literal: One revolution of the ground wheels, and the distance traveled on the ground is three paces.
translations.idiomatic: One revolution of the ground wheels advances the carriage three paces.

sentences.zh: 以古法六尺為步，三百步為裏，用較今法五尺為步，三百六十步為裏。

translations.literal: By the ancient method six chi make one pace, three hundred paces make one li; comparing with the present method five chi make one pace, three hundred sixty paces make one li.
translations.idiomatic: By the ancient reckoning six chi made one pace and three hundred paces one li; by the present reckoning five chi make one pace and three hundred sixty paces one li.

sentences.zh: 立輪一，附於左足，徑一尺三寸八分，圍四尺一寸四分，出齒十八，齒間相去二寸三分。

translations.literal: One upright wheel, attached to the left ground wheel; diameter one chi three cun eight fen, circumference four chi one cun four fen; projecting teeth eighteen; between teeth two cun three fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: One upright wheel attached to the left ground wheel is one chi three cun eight fen in diameter with a circumference of four chi one cun four fen, bearing eighteen teeth spaced two cun three fen apart.

sentences.zh: 下平輪一，其徑四尺一寸四分，圍一丈二尺四寸二分，出齒五十四，齒間相去與附立輪同。

translations.literal: One lower flat wheel; its diameter four chi one cun four fen, circumference one zhang two chi four cun two fen; projecting teeth fifty-four; between teeth the spacing is the same as the attached upright wheel.
translations.idiomatic: One lower flat wheel is four chi one cun four fen in diameter with a circumference of one zhang two chi four cun two fen, bearing fifty-four teeth spaced the same as those on the attached upright wheel.

sentences.zh: 立貫心軸一，其上設銅旋風輪一，出齒三，齒間相去一寸二分。

translations.literal: One upright through-heart axle; above it is set one bronze whirlwind wheel; projecting teeth three; between teeth one cun two fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: One upright through-heart axle bears above it a bronze whirlwind wheel with three projecting teeth spaced one cun two fen apart.

sentences.zh: 中立平輪一，其徑四尺，圍一丈二尺，出齒百，齒間相去與旋風等。

translations.literal: At the center one upright flat wheel; its diameter four chi, circumference one zhang two chi; projecting teeth one hundred; between teeth the spacing equals that of the whirlwind wheel.
translations.idiomatic: At the center stands one upright flat wheel four chi in diameter with a circumference of one zhang two chi, bearing one hundred teeth spaced the same as those on the whirlwind wheel.

sentences.zh: 次安小平輪一，其徑三寸少半寸，圍一尺，出齒十，齒間相去一寸半。

translations.literal: Next affixed one small flat wheel; its diameter three cun less half a cun, circumference one chi; projecting teeth ten; between teeth one cun half apart.
translations.idiomatic: Next is affixed one small flat wheel two and a half cun in diameter with a circumference of one chi, bearing ten teeth spaced one cun and a half apart.

sentences.zh: 上平輪一，其徑三尺少半尺，圍一丈，出齒百，齒間相去與小平輪同。

translations.literal: One upper flat wheel; its diameter three chi less half a chi, circumference one zhang; projecting teeth one hundred; between teeth the spacing is the same as the small flat wheel.
translations.idiomatic: One upper flat wheel is two and a half chi in diameter with a circumference of one zhang, bearing one hundred teeth spaced the same as those on the small flat wheel.

sentences.zh: 其中平輪轉一周，車行一里，下一層木人擊鼓；

translations.literal: When the central flat wheel turns one revolution, the carriage travels one li, and the lower-tier wooden figure strikes the drum;
translations.idiomatic: When the central flat wheel completes one revolution the carriage has traveled one li, and the lower-tier wooden figure strikes the drum;

sentences.zh: 上平輪轉一周，車行十里，上一層木人擊鐲。

translations.literal: When the upper flat wheel turns one revolution, the carriage travels ten li, and the upper-tier wooden figure strikes the gong.
translations.idiomatic: when the upper flat wheel completes one revolution the carriage has traveled ten li, and the upper-tier wooden figure strikes the gong.

sentences.zh: 凡用大小輪八，合二百八十五齒，遞相鉤鎖，犬牙相製，周而復始。”

translations.literal: In all use large and small wheels eight; in total two hundred eighty-five teeth; successively interlocking, intermeshing like dog's teeth to constrain one another, cycling and beginning again."
translations.idiomatic: In all it employs eight large and small wheels with two hundred eighty-five teeth in total, interlocking and meshing in succession in an endless cycle.

sentences.zh: 詔以其法下有司製之。

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.) An edict ordered that this method be transmitted to the responsible offices for manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: (Closing quotation mark in the source.) An edict then ordered the responsible offices to manufacture it according to this method.

sentences.zh: 大觀之製，車箱上下為兩層，上安木人二，身各手執木槌。

translations.literal: The Daguan design: the carriage box upper and lower formed two tiers; above two wooden figures were affixed, each in person holding a wooden mallet.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Daguan design the carriage box had upper and lower tiers, above which stood two wooden figures, each holding a wooden mallet.

sentences.zh: 輪軸共四。

translations.literal: Wheel axles four in all.
translations.idiomatic: There were four wheel axles in all.

sentences.zh: 內左壁車腳上立輪一，安在車箱內，徑二尺二寸五分，圍六尺七寸五分，二十齒，齒間相去三寸三分五厘。

translations.literal: On the inner left wall one wheel stood upright on the carriage leg, set within the carriage box; diameter two chi two cun five fen, circumference six chi seven cun five fen; twenty teeth; between teeth three cun three fen five li apart.
translations.idiomatic: On the inner left wall, one wheel stood upright on the carriage leg inside the box, two chi two cun five fen in diameter with a circumference of six chi seven cun five fen, bearing twenty teeth spaced three cun three fen five li apart.

sentences.zh: 又平輪一，徑四尺六寸五分，圍一丈三尺九寸五分，出齒六十，齒間相去二寸四分。

translations.literal: Further one flat wheel; diameter four chi six cun five fen, circumference one zhang three chi nine cun five fen; projecting teeth sixty; between teeth two cun four fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: There is also one flat wheel, four chi six cun five fen in diameter with a circumference of one zhang three chi nine cun five fen, bearing sixty teeth spaced two cun four fen apart.

sentences.zh: 上大平輪一，通軸貫上，徑三尺八寸，圍一丈一尺，出齒一百，齒間相去一寸二分。

translations.literal: One upper large flat wheel; a through-axle passes up through it; diameter three chi eight cun, circumference one zhang one chi; projecting teeth one hundred; between teeth one cun two fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: One upper large flat wheel is pierced by a through-axle, three chi eight cun in diameter with a circumference of one zhang one chi, bearing one hundred teeth spaced one cun two fen apart.

sentences.zh: 立軸一，徑二寸二分，圍六寸六分，出齒三，齒間相去二寸二分。

translations.literal: One upright axle; diameter two cun two fen, circumference six cun six fen; projecting teeth three; between teeth two cun two fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: One upright axle is two cun two fen in diameter with a circumference of six cun six fen, bearing three teeth spaced two cun two fen apart.

sentences.zh: 外大平輪軸上有鐵撥子二。

translations.literal: On the outer large flat wheel axle are two iron triggers.
translations.idiomatic: On the outer large flat wheel axle are two iron triggers.

sentences.zh: 又木橫軸上關戾、撥子各一。

translations.literal: Further on the wooden cross-axle one latch mechanism and one trigger each.
translations.idiomatic: On the wooden cross-axle are one latch mechanism and one trigger each.

sentences.zh: 其車腳轉一百遭，通輪軸轉周，木人各一擊鉦、鼓。

translations.literal: When the carriage legs turn one hundred revolutions, the through wheel axles turn one full cycle, and each wooden figure strikes the gong and drum once.
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage legs complete one hundred revolutions, the through wheel axles make one full cycle, and each wooden figure strikes the gong and drum once.

sentences.zh: 白鷺車，隋所製也，一名鼓吹車。

translations.literal: The White Egret Carriage: a Sui design, also called the Acclaim-and-Drums Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The white egret carriage was a Sui design, also called the acclaim-and-drums carriage.

sentences.zh: 赤質，周施花版，上有朱柱，貫五輪相重，輪衣以緋，皂頂及緋絡帶，並繡飛鷺。

translations.literal: Red substance; floral panels encircled it all around; above were vermilion pillars threading five overlapping wheels; wheel covers of scarlet; black crown and scarlet luo belts, all embroidered with flying egrets.
translations.idiomatic: It was red in substance, encircled with floral panels; vermilion pillars above threaded five overlapping wheels; its scarlet wheel covers, black crown, and scarlet luo belts were all embroidered with flying egrets.

sentences.zh: 柱杪刻木為鷺，銜鵝毛筒，紅綬帶。

translations.literal: At the pillar tips wood was carved into egrets, holding goose-feather tubes; red ribbon sashes.
translations.idiomatic: At the pillar tips stood egrets carved from wood, holding goose-feather tubes with red ribbon sashes.

sentences.zh: 一轅。

translations.literal: One yoke.
translations.idiomatic: It had a single yoke.

sentences.zh: 駕四馬，駕士十八人。

translations.literal: Drawn by four horses; carriage attendants eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by four horses and attended by eighteen drivers.

sentences.zh: 鸞旗車，漢製，為前驅。

translations.literal: The Luan-Banner Carriage: a Han design, serving as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The luan-banner carriage was a Han design that served as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 赤質，曲壁，一轅。

translations.literal: Red substance; curved walls; one yoke.
translations.idiomatic: It was red in substance, with curved walls and a single yoke.

sentences.zh: 上載赤旗，繡鸞鳥。

translations.literal: Above it bore a red banner embroidered with luan birds.
translations.idiomatic: It bore a red banner embroidered with luan birds on its top.

sentences.zh: 駕四馬，駕士十八人。

translations.literal: Drawn by four horses; carriage attendants eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by four horses and attended by eighteen drivers.

sentences.zh: 皮軒車，漢前驅車也。

translations.literal: The Leather Canopy Carriage: a Han vanguard carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The leather canopy carriage was a Han vanguard carriage.

sentences.zh: 冒以虎皮為軒，取《曲禮》“前有士師，則載虎皮”之義，赤質，曲壁，上有柱，貫五輪相重，畫虎文。

translations.literal: Covered with a tiger-hide canopy, taking the meaning from the Classic of Rites (Qu Li), "If a military commander goes before, then display the tiger hide"; red substance, curved walls; above were pillars threading five overlapping wheels, painted with tiger patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Its canopy was of tiger hide, following the Qu Li passage "If a military commander goes before, then display the tiger hide"; it was red in substance with curved walls; pillars above threaded five overlapping wheels painted with tiger patterns.

sentences.zh: 駕四馬，駕士十八人。

translations.literal: Drawn by four horses; carriage attendants eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by four horses and attended by eighteen drivers.

sentences.zh: 政和之製，用漆柱，貫朱漆皮軒五。

translations.literal: The Zhenghe design: lacquered pillars, threading five vermilion-lacquered leather canopies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe design it used lacquered pillars threading five vermilion-lacquered leather canopies.

sentences.zh: 黃鉞車，漢製，乘輿建之，在大駕後。

translations.literal: The Yellow Battle-Axe Carriage: a Han design; the imperial carriage raised it, positioned behind the great procession.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow battle-axe carriage was a Han design; it was raised at the imperial carriage and placed behind the great procession.

sentences.zh: 晉鹵簿有黃鉞車。

translations.literal: The Jin guard of honor included the yellow battle-axe carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin imperial guard included the yellow battle-axe carriage.

sentences.zh: 唐初無之，貞觀後始加。

translations.literal: Early Tang lacked it; only after the Zhenguan era was it added.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang lacked it; it was added only after the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 赤質，曲壁，中設金鉞一，錦囊綢杠。

translations.literal: Red substance, curved walls; in the center was set one golden battle-axe; brocade bag and silk pole.
translations.idiomatic: It was red in substance with curved walls; a golden battle-axe stood at the center, with a brocade bag and silk pole.

sentences.zh: 左武衛隊正一人，在車中執鉞。

translations.literal: One squad leader of the Left Martial Guard, within the carriage holding the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: One squad leader of the Left Martial Guard rode in the carriage holding the battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 駕兩馬，駕士十五人。

translations.literal: Drawn by two horses; carriage attendants fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by two horses and attended by fifteen drivers.

sentences.zh: 豹尾車。

translations.literal: The Leopard-Tail Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The leopard-tail carriage.

sentences.zh: 古者軍正建豹尾。

translations.literal: In antiquity the army commander raised the leopard tail.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the army commander raised the leopard tail.

sentences.zh: 漢製，最後車一乘垂豹尾，豹尾以前即同禁中。

translations.literal: Han design: the last carriage of one team bore the hanging leopard tail; before the leopard tail was the same as within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han design the rearmost carriage of the train bore the hanging leopard tail; everything before the leopard tail counted as within the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀後，始加此車於鹵簿內，製同黃鉞車。

translations.literal: After Tang's Zhenguan era, this carriage was first added within the guard of honor; its design matched the yellow battle-axe carriage.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhenguan era Tang added this carriage to the guard of honor; its design matched the yellow battle-axe carriage.

sentences.zh: 上戴朱漆竿，首綴豹尾，右武衛隊正一人執之。

translations.literal: Above it bore a vermilion-lacquered pole; at the top was affixed a leopard tail; one squad leader of the Right Martial Guard held it.
translations.idiomatic: It bore a vermilion-lacquered pole topped with a leopard tail, held by one squad leader of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 駕兩馬，駕士十五人。

translations.literal: Drawn by two horses; carriage attendants fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by two horses and attended by fifteen drivers.

sentences.zh: 屬車，一曰副車，一曰貳車，一曰左車。

translations.literal: The retinue carriage: also called the secondary carriage, the reserve carriage, the left carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The retinue carriage was also called the secondary carriage, the reserve carriage, or the left carriage.

sentences.zh: 秦製，大駕屬車八十一乘，法駕三十六乘。

translations.literal: Qin design: in the great procession retinue carriages eighty-one teams; in the statutory procession thirty-six teams.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin design the great procession included eighty-one retinue carriages and the statutory procession thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 漢法駕用三十一乘，小駕用十二乘。

translations.literal: Han statutory procession used thirty-one teams; minor procession used twelve teams.
translations.idiomatic: The Han statutory procession used thirty-one carriages and the minor procession twelve.

sentences.zh: 隋製，大駕三十六，法駕十二，小駕不用。

translations.literal: Sui design: great procession thirty-six; statutory twelve; minor procession did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui design the great procession used thirty-six, the statutory twelve, and the minor procession none.

sentences.zh: 唐大駕唯用十二乘，宋因之。

translations.literal: Tang great procession used only twelve teams; Song followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang great procession used only twelve carriages, and Song followed suit.

sentences.zh: 黑質，兩箱軬裝，前有曲闌，金銅飾，上施紫通幰，絡帶、門簾皆繡雲鶴，紫絲網分錔。

translations.literal: Black substance; double box with curtained enclosure; before it curved railings; gold and bronze ornament; above was set a purple through-canopy; luo belts and door curtains all embroidered with cloud-cranes; purple silk net with corner plates.
translations.idiomatic: It was black in substance, with a double box and curtained sides, curved railings before it, and gold and bronze ornament; a purple through-canopy hung above, with luo belts and door curtains embroidered with cloud-cranes and a purple silk net with corner plates.

sentences.zh: 每乘駕三牛，駕士十人。

translations.literal: Each team drawn by three oxen; carriage attendants ten.
translations.idiomatic: Each carriage was drawn by three oxen and attended by ten drivers.

sentences.zh: 五車。

translations.literal: The Five Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The five carriages.

sentences.zh: 徽宗宣和元年，禮製局言：“舊鹵簿記有白鷺、鸞旗、皮軒三車，其製非古。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe under Emperor Huizong, the Ritual Design Bureau stated: "The old records of the guard of honor include the white egret, luan-banner, and leather canopy carriages—their designs are not ancient.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuanhe reign, the Ritual Design Bureau reported to Emperor Huizong: "The old guard-of-honor records list the white egret, luan-banner, and leather canopy carriages, but their designs are not ancient.

sentences.zh: 按《曲禮》曰：‘前有水則載青旌，前有塵埃則載鳴鳶，前有車騎則載飛鴻，前有士師則載虎皮，前有鷙獸則載貔貅。

translations.literal: According to the Classic of Rites (Qu Li) it says: 'If there is water ahead, then display the green banner; if there is dust ahead, then display the crying kite; if there are chariots and horsemen ahead, then display the flying wild goose; if there is a military commander ahead, then display the tiger hide; if there are fierce beasts ahead, then display the pixiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Qu Li states: "If water lies ahead, carry the green banner; if dust rises ahead, carry the crying-kite banner; if chariots and horsemen approach ahead, carry the flying-wild-goose banner; if a military commander goes before, carry the tiger hide; if fierce beasts lie ahead, carry the pixiu banner.

sentences.zh: ’萬乘一出，五車必載，所以警眾也。

translations.literal: 'When the lord of ten thousand chariots goes forth, the five carriages must be borne, thereby to alert the masses.
translations.idiomatic: When the lord of ten thousand chariots goes forth, the five carriages must always be carried, to warn the people.

sentences.zh: 青旌、鳴鳶、飛鴻、貔貅乃以白鷺、鸞旗雜陳其間，未為合禮。

translations.literal: The green banner, crying kite, flying wild goose, and pixiu were rather mixed in among the white egret and luan-banner, not conforming to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the green banner, crying kite, flying wild goose, and pixiu were jumbled among the white egret and luan-banner carriages—not in keeping with ritual.

sentences.zh: 今欲改五車相次於中道，繼之以崇德車，於是為備。”

translations.literal: Now we wish to reorder the five carriages in succession along the central road, followed by the Honoring Virtue Carriage—then the array will be complete.
translations.idiomatic: We propose to array the five carriages in succession along the central road, followed by the Honoring Virtue Carriage, and the procession will then be complete."

sentences.zh: 青旌車，赤質，曲壁，中載青旌，以絳帛為之，書青鳥於其上。

translations.literal: The Green Banner Carriage: red substance, curved walls; at the center it bore the green banner, made of deep-red silk, with blue birds written upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The green banner carriage was red in substance with curved walls; it bore a green banner of deep-red silk emblazoned with blue birds at the center.

sentences.zh: 鳴鳶車，赤質，曲壁，中載鳴鳶旌，以絳帛為之，畫鳴鳶於其上。

translations.literal: The Crying-Kite Carriage: red substance, curved walls; at the center it bore the crying-kite banner, made of deep-red silk, with a crying kite painted upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The crying-kite carriage was red in substance with curved walls; it bore a crying-kite banner of deep-red silk painted with a crying kite at the center.

sentences.zh: 飛鴻車，赤質，曲壁，中載飛鴻旌，以絳帛為之，畫飛鴻於其上。

translations.literal: The Flying-Wild-Goose Carriage: red substance, curved walls; at the center it bore the flying-wild-goose banner, made of deep-red silk, with a flying wild goose painted upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The flying-wild-goose carriage was red in substance with curved walls; it bore a flying-wild-goose banner of deep-red silk painted with a flying wild goose at the center.

sentences.zh: 虎皮車，赤質，曲壁，中載虎皮旌，以絳帛為之，緣以赤，畫虎皮於上。

translations.literal: The Tiger-Hide Carriage: red substance, curved walls; at the center it bore the tiger-hide banner, made of deep-red silk, bordered with red, with a tiger hide painted upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger-hide carriage was red in substance with curved walls; it bore a tiger-hide banner of deep-red silk bordered in red and painted with a tiger hide at the center.

sentences.zh: 貔貅車，赤質，曲壁，旌以絳帛為之，緣以赤，畫貔貅於上。

translations.literal: The Pixiu Carriage: red substance, curved walls; the banner made of deep-red silk, bordered with red, with a pixiu painted upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The pixiu carriage was red in substance with curved walls; its banner was of deep-red silk bordered in red and painted with a pixiu.

sentences.zh: 其轅皆一。

translations.literal: Their yokes were all one each.
translations.idiomatic: Each had a single yoke.

sentences.zh: 涼車，赤質，金塗銀裝，龍鳳五采明金，織以紅黃藤，油壁，緋絲絛龍頭，梅紅羅褥，銀螭頭，穗球，雲朵踏頭，蓮花坐，雁鉤，火珠，門遝，𨧱鉞，頻伽，大小鐶，駕以橐駝。

translations.literal: The Cooling Carriage: red substance; gold-plated silver fittings; dragon-and-phoenix five-color bright gold; woven with red and yellow rattan; oil-painted walls; scarlet silk-cord dragon heads, plum-red gauze cushions, silver chi-dragon heads, tassel balls, cloud-pattern tread heads, lotus seats, wild-goose hooks, fire pearls, door latches, sa-yue ornaments, kalavinkas, large and small rings; drawn by camels.
translations.idiomatic: The cooling carriage was red in substance with gold-plated silver fittings and dragon-and-phoenix five-color bright gold, woven with red and yellow rattan and oil-painted walls; it bore scarlet silk-cord dragon heads, plum-red gauze cushions, silver chi-dragon heads, tassel balls, cloud-pattern tread heads, lotus seats, wild-goose hooks, fire pearls, door latches, sa-yue ornaments, kalavinkas, and large and small rings, and was drawn by camels.

sentences.zh: 省方在道及校獵回則乘之。

translations.literal: On provincial tours while on the road and on returning from hunts it was ridden.
translations.idiomatic: It was used on provincial tours while traveling and when returning from the hunt.

sentences.zh: 相風烏輿，上載長竿，竿杪刻木為烏，垂鵝毛筒，紅綬帶，下承以小盤，周以緋裙，繡烏形。

translations.literal: The Wind-Measuring Bird Carriage: above it bore a long pole; at the pole tip wood was carved into a bird, with goose-feather tubes hanging down and red ribbon sashes; below supported by a small dish; encircled with a scarlet skirt embroidered with bird forms.
translations.idiomatic: The wind-measuring bird carriage bore a long pole; at its tip stood a bird carved from wood, with goose-feather tubes and red ribbon sashes hanging down; a small dish supported it below, and a scarlet skirt embroidered with bird forms encircled it.

sentences.zh: 輿士四人。

translations.literal: Carriage bearers four.
translations.idiomatic: Four bearers attended it.

sentences.zh: 行漏輿，隋大業行漏車也。

translations.literal: The Moving Clepsydra Carriage: the Sui Daye moving clepsydra carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The moving clepsydra carriage derived from the Sui Daye moving clepsydra carriage.

sentences.zh: 製同鍾、鼓樓而大，設刻漏如稱衡。

translations.literal: Its design matched the bell and drum tower carriages but was larger; a graduated clepsydra was set up like a balance steelyard.
translations.idiomatic: Its design matched the bell and drum towers but on a larger scale, with a graduated clepsydra set like a steelyard balance.

sentences.zh: 首垂銅缽，末有銅象，漆匱貯水，渴烏注水入缽中。

translations.literal: At the front hung a bronze bowl; at the end was a bronze elephant; a lacquer case stored water; a siphon bird poured water into the bowl.
translations.idiomatic: A bronze bowl hung at the front; a bronze elephant stood at the rear; a lacquer case held the water, and a siphon bird poured it into the bowl.

sentences.zh: 長竿四，輿士六十人。

translations.literal: Long poles four; carriage bearers sixty.
translations.idiomatic: It had four long poles and was attended by sixty bearers.

sentences.zh: 十二神輿，赤質，四門旁刻十二辰神，緋繡輪衣、絡帶。

translations.literal: The Twelve Spirit Carriage: red substance; at the four doors were carved the twelve zodiac deities; scarlet embroidered wheel covers and luo belts.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve spirit carriage was red in substance; the twelve zodiac deities were carved beside its four doors, with scarlet embroidered wheel covers and luo belts.

sentences.zh: 輿士十二人。

translations.literal: Carriage bearers twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve bearers attended it.

sentences.zh: 交龍鉦、鼓輿各一，皆刻木為二青龍相交，下有木台、長竿，一掛畫鼓，一掛金鉦，上皆有緋蓋，亦繡交龍。

translations.literal: Interlocking-Dragon gong and drum carriages one each; all carved wood into two azure dragons interlocking; below were wooden platforms and long poles; one hung a painted drum, one hung a golden gong; above both were scarlet canopies, also embroidered with interlocking dragons.
translations.idiomatic: There was one interlocking-dragon gong carriage and one drum carriage; each was carved from wood as two azure dragons interlocking, with a wooden platform and long pole below; one hung a painted drum and the other a golden gong; both bore scarlet canopies embroidered with interlocking dragons.

sentences.zh: 輿士各二人。

translations.literal: Carriage bearers two each.
translations.idiomatic: Each was attended by two bearers.

sentences.zh: 中興後，相風、行漏、十二神、鉦鼓四輿，悉省去。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, the wind-measuring, moving clepsydra, twelve spirit, and gong-drum four carriages were all eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration the wind-measuring, moving clepsydra, twelve spirit, and gong-drum carriages—all four—were entirely cut from the procession.

sentences.zh: 鍾、鼓樓輿各一，本隋大駕鍾車、鼓車也。

translations.literal: Bell and drum tower carriages one each; originally the Sui great procession bell carriage and drum carriage.
translations.idiomatic: There was one bell tower carriage and one drum tower carriage, originally the Sui great-procession bell carriage and drum carriage.

sentences.zh: 皆刻木為屋，中置鍾、鼓，下施木台、長竿，如鉦、鼓輿。

translations.literal: All carved wood into houses; within were set bell and drum; below were affixed wooden platforms and long poles, like the gong and drum carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Each was carved from wood into a house shape with a bell or drum set within, and a wooden platform and long pole below, like the gong and drum carriages.

sentences.zh: 輿士各二十四人。

translations.literal: Carriage bearers twenty-four each.
translations.idiomatic: Each was attended by twenty-four bearers.

sentences.zh: 行漏輿、十二神輿、交龍鉦鼓輿、鍾鼓樓，舊禮無文，皆太祖開寶定禮所增。

translations.literal: The moving clepsydra carriage, twelve spirit carriage, interlocking-dragon gong-drum carriage, and bell-drum towers: the old rites had no record of them; all were additions made when Emperor Taizu fixed the rites in the Kaibao era.
translations.idiomatic: The moving clepsydra carriage, twelve spirit carriage, interlocking-dragon gong-drum carriage, and bell-drum towers had no precedent in the old rites; all were additions made when Emperor Taizu established the rites in the Kaibao era.
